No hats or sneakers allowed.

description: Monday night can get a little crazy at this Scottsdale hangout, as DJ Steel starts the workweek off with his eclectic mix of classic and indie-rock, as well as plenty of electro beats.

name: Electrostatic
description: This hipster dance party used to draw huge crowds to both Glam and the Homme Lounge, but now that those clubs have closed, DJ Joshie and Benni Beatnik have moved their Tuesday night party to this new central Phoenix hotspot. Spinning a mix of nu-disco, drum 'n' bass, dubstep and indie-rock, the night also features DJs Bigie, the Ariel and Kid Turnswell.

Expect plenty of guests to hit the decks alongside Pickster, including Meaty Ogre, Brad B. from the Drunken Immortals and Tenski. Event runs every other Tuesday.

name: Young Sounds of Arizona
description: This big band features 40 students from more than 20 schools in the Phoenix area. Formed in 1971, the group continues to highlight young, local talent. The band performs classic jazz standards and big-band hits.

name: Pinnacle Concert Series: Harry James Orchestra
description: One of the biggest names of the big band era, Harry James was well known for his trumpet virtuosity; his wife, Betty Grable; and his lead singer, Frank Sinatra. Though James died in 1983, the Harry James Orchestra has continued his trademark sound with mellow arrangements and a complex rhythm section, performing under the direction of trumpet virtuoso Fred Radke.

name: Pinnacle Concert Series: Groove for Thought
description: This seven-piece Seattle vocal group has been pleasing crowds around the country with a soulful blend of jazz and R&B. The group performs original songs, along with tunes by Billy Joel and Bill Withers.

name: Willowbrook Performing Arts Series: Desert Brass Band
description: The Desert Brass Band performs an evening of classic big-band music, including hits from the 1940s and '50s, under the direction of Charles Musgrave.

name: Pinnacle Concert Series: Dixieland Ramblers
description: Formed in 1957 by clarinetist Mike Bennett and drummer Tom Stevenson, this band combines New Orleans jazz, swing and mainstream jazz styles. The group has released four albums and performs their tunes on piano, bass, drums, clarinet, trumpet and trombone.

name: Fred Forney’s Arizona Jazz Masterworks Orchestra: "They Came to Swing!"
description: Trumpeter Fred Forney leads the Arizona Jazz Masterworks Orchestra in a big-band celebration of Duke Ellington, Count Basie, Benny Goodman, Jelly Roll Morton and many more. The show includes new works by contemporary composers Vince Mendoza, John Clayton, Bob Brookmeyer and Maria Schneider.

name: Ken Waldman: Alaska's Fiddling Poet
description: Old-time fiddle music is paired with original poetry from storyteller, Ken Waldman.

description: Local jazz favorite and Arizona Blues Hall of Famer Margo Reed teams up with Armand Boatman and the Be Bop Revolution for a night of high-energy jazz. The group performs material by Charlie Parker, Bud Powell, Dizzy Gillespie, Tadd Dameron and Hank Mobley, as well as original swing and bob songs.

On Sundays, Stickweeds opens their doors with local acoustic blues players for a blues brunch. Coffee and danishes are offered. Everyone is welcome to come and enjoy the show.

description: This multimedia tribute honors Rock and Roll Hall of Famer Ricky Nelson, who died in a plane crash in 1985. The singer's twin sons, Matthew and Gunnar, perform of some of Nelson's biggest hits, including "Hello Mary Lou," "Travelin' Man" and "Garden Party."

name: The Pink Floyd Experience
description: Re-creating the classic music of beloved psychedelic rock pioneers Pink Floyd, this world-renown tribute band offers an over-the-top stage show to match. The show features six musicians playing songs such as "Money,” “Wish You Were Here,” “Time,” “Comfortably Numb” and “Another Brick in the Wall,” accompanied by interpretive videos, plane crashes, a flying pig, a helicopter and other stage stunts.

name: Hotel California: A Salute to the Eagles
description: The band pays tribute to the classic rockers whose sound incorporates elements of country and R&B. Hear hits by the Eagles, including "Hotel California," "Take It Easy," "Heartache Tonight" and "Love Will Keep Us Alive."

name: Xtra Ticket
description: Thursday nights, jam out to the songs of the Grateful Dead with Tempe tribute band Xtra Ticket. Each character in the group, which has been together since 1994, takes on a character from the Grateful Dead, creating faithful re-creations of some of the band's most iconic songs.

name: The Train Tracks
description: Train Tracks is a foray into local live music in Phoenix via the light rail, held on the first Friday of each month. This is a way to check out fresh, collective top notch bands from the music scene as they perform live on the light rail. So jump on any Friday and check it out. Check Web Site for times.

name: Train Tracks Plugged In
description: Downtown Phoenix hosts this monthly concert series in the park featuring local bands of various musical genres every third Friday of the month through 2009.

name: Third Friday Concert in the Park
description: Bring your friends along with a chair or blanket and enjoy the sights and sounds of a local band in the Downtown Civic Space Park. The concert is part of the Third Friday Concert in the Park series. Check the Web site to hear which band is featured for that month. Located near the ASU campus.

location: Mill Ave. and University Drive Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Music On Mill
description: Musicians and performers of all sorts line the streets throughout the district giving visitors a variety of entertainment. Mill Avenue is where historic music venues such as Long Wong's, Gibson's and Edsel's Attic were located at one time that became the launchpads for bands such as the Gin Blossoms, the Refreshments, Dead Hot Workshop and Jimmy Eat World. Branded donation paint cans that are placed at each of their locations identify musicians scheduled to perform for Music on Mill.

name: Brian Demarco Trio
description: Every Sunday afternoon, these Phoenix roots rockers perform at the Postino brunch, playing covers and tunes from their latest album, "Solitary Bird."

name: Elvis Before Noon
description: This local band specializes in the kind of indie-rock power-pop that landed Tempe bands like the Refreshments and Gin Blossoms on the national stage in the 1990s. Dedicated to carrying on that “Tempe sound,” the band features Scott Johnson, a Gin Blossoms member. Visitors can also enjoy half-priced bottles of wine every Sunday.

location: 7330 N. Dreamy Draw Drive Phoenix, AZ, 85020

name: Brendon Cotrell
description: With a distinctive baritone voice, this Phoenix singer-songwriter crafts dreamy indie-rock tunes full of dark melodies and sparkling, romantic touches. Cotrell released his debut album, "Rough Cuts," in 2010 and is already working on his followup, “These Walls Were Meant For Climbing.” He also published his first children’s book “Ruby’s Rainy Day” in 2010. Cotrell plays at RA Sushi Sunday evenings.

description: These Buddhist monks chant, dance and play such instruments as the 10-foot long dung-chen horn. The group showcases the Tibetan culture and its traditions. They have been endorsed by the Dalai Lama as a means of promoting world peace and healing through sacred performing art.

name: Paco Pena's Flamenco Sin Fronteras

description: Guitarist Paco Pena joins a dozen other virtuoso musicians and a group of flamenco dancers to showcase the music and dance that evolved out of the migration of Spanish performers to Latin America.

name: Street Beat
description: This high-energy performance troupe features creator Ben Hansen and 10 drummers, dancers and musicians, who showcase urban life, using hip-hop moves, urban percussion and rhythms, and break dancing. Bringing the sounds and moves of urban culture to the stage, critics have called Street Beat's show "an urbanized journey through percussion."

name: Sierra Leone’s Refugee All Stars
description: The group took to the stage in 2006 after the debut of a documentary film that highlighted their formation in a West African refugee camp. The musicians transcended their humble beginnings and have been successful, receiving critical acclaim for their first full-length release, “Living Like a Refugee." The album's title track was recorded by the light of an oil lamp at the refugee camp.

name: The Diamonds

name: "Otello"
description: The Arizona Opera presents this classic four-act opera by Giuseppe Verdi, based on Shakespeare's "Othello." The opera tells the story of Otello, a warrior who returns home from battle and is now the governor of Cyprus. But Otello has made a deadly enemy in the treacherous Iago, who pretends to be his friend. As Iago spins a web of lies, Otello begins to doubt the faithfulness of his beloved wife, Desdemona. Caught between lying whispers and his own paranoia, Otello must decide what he truly believes. Sung in Italian with English supertitles.

description: This 300-member children's chorus performs an evening of classic and contemporary classical works. The evening features singers ranging in age from 7 to 18.

description: This free performance features a performance by acclaimed organist Philip Smith, who has performed throughout Scandinavia, England, Germany and the U.S., and serves as the organ curator of the Walt Disney Concert Hall in Los Angeles.

"Live & Let Die: The Music of Paul McCartney"
Solemn Evensong
description: The Cathedral Choir performs Solemn Evensong in celebration of Trinity Sunday. Solemn Evensong is a long-standing tradition in the Anglican church. The performance is followed by a reception in the Olney Gallery.

location: 700 W. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Lynne Aspnes and John Wickey
description: Duo harpists Lynne Aspnes and John Wickey perform selections from Bach, Mendelssohn and Ravel. Part of the “Performance with A View” series which offers informative, entertaining and informal performances by guest artists from a variety of artistic disciplines. Held in the Lakeside Room.

name: Blunt Club
description: Presented by Dumperfoo and Doug the Professional, this weekly hip-hop night is now in its ninth year and has attracted a devoted following. The Blunt Club decided to leave their Club Red home after two years in 2010, but they're still spinning some of the best hip-hop, funk, drum and bass, dubstep and glitch-hop. Over the years, the weekly dance night has attracted guest DJs from around the country, including Afrika Bambaataa, DJ Joe Nice and Public Enemy.

name: DJ Top Cat
description: The oldest tiki bar in Phoenix since the mid '40s brings DJ Top Cat to spin an eclectic mix of ska/punk/psychobilly/spy surf and plain old rock and roll every Sunday and Wednesday night. Find a booth and hide away with drink specials and other stranded castaways.

name: Obscura
description: Resident DJs Roya and Funkfinger entertain by spinning Britpop, indie, '80s new wave and mod tunes. The dance party highlights upcoming CD releases. Drink specials include $3 well drinks and $2 house pints. Age 21 and older.

name: Noche de Salsa
description: Features salsa lessons at 9 p.m. and open salsa dancing with guest DJs spinning music at 10 p.m.

name: DJ Swerve and DJ Phantom
description: Drink specials: $2 Vodka Socko, wells and Anheiser Bush.

name: Tim Eriksen
description: Regarded as one of the finest ballad singers working today, Eriksen combines the sounds of Americana, Appalachia and Irish folk songs with classic punk rock, wrapping them up with his distinctive voice and arrangements for fiddle, banjo, guitar and bajo sexto. The Massachusetts native is also a member of the punk-folk band Cordelia's Dad, which has toured with groups such as Nirvana, Uncle Tupelo, and Weezer.

name: Axis/Radius
description: The bilevel clubs joined by a glass catwalk complement each other in sound and energy. Radius offers techno and Top 40, while the more subdued Axis concentrates on a broad selection of sounds. Axis/Radius also offers exotic food and drinks, a cigar bar and the Amber Lounge VIP club. Special events and Ladies' Night on Thursdays also are featured.

name: Pinnacle Concert Series: "Time Out for the Arts: Way Over in Beulah Lan’"
description: Mezzo-soprano Jennifer Allen and Pinnacle Presbyterian Church's music director Brent Hylton present this exploration of the spirituals and folk songs sung by African slaves.

name: Sky Lounge
description: Sky is known for staying open past normal bar and club hours, as well as being party central to those who want to dance to hip hop, Latin- and Spanish-inspired music.

location: 13243 N. Founders Park Blvd. Surprise, AZ, 85379

location: Sheraton Phoenix Downtown Hotel 320 N. Third St. Phoenix, AZ, 85004
name: Jazz Trio/DJ Senbad Fridays
venue: District American Kitchen and Wine Bar
description: Kick off your Friday night with a live performance by a jazz trio from 5 p.m. to 10 p.m. Then stay for the smooth house beats of DJ Senbad at 9 p.m. Drink specials are offered all night.

name: West Valley Arts Council: Burnett Family Bluegrass
description: This five-piece family bluegrass band hails from the mountains of Northern Arizona, and since their formation in 1993, the group has been wowing audiences around the country, taking home the coveted top prize at the 2004 Telluride Bluegrass Festival band competition. The band released their second album, "Bend the Wind," in 2005.

name: Club Dwntwn
description: This downtown-Phoenix nightclub features resident DJs RO55 and Kathryn. Check out Friday night's Lushlife, with dance-rock, post-punk, Britpop, Indie and new-wave songs from 10 p.m.-3:30 a.m. Saturday night is Latin night, with DJs spinning Latin pop, salsa and merengue. Dress code is enforced.

name: Lushlife
description: Resident DJs R055 and Kathryn play dance rock, post punk, britpop, indie and new wave songs.

name: Tranzylvania
description: Arizona's largest goth/industrial club. DJs spin EBM, gothic, industrial and synthpop music. For ages 21 and older from 10 p.m.-2 a.m. For ages 18 and older from 2-3:30 a.m.

DJ's Djentrification, Meaty Ogre, Salchi von Papi and Matty P man the decks, spinning everything from indie rock and hip-hop, to psychedelia and funk from Thailand.

name: The Shop
description: Underground hip-hop/old-school music spun by DJ Al Page and guests.

name: Ransom
description: Every Friday this divey Phoenix bar transforms into a dance floor heaven, with resident DJs Kevin M.O.B., Craig Citizen, Bigie and Benni Beatnik spinning some of the hottest tunes of the 1980s and '90s.

name: Cheap Thrills
description: The dance floor at this Saturday night party features beautiful people moving to the hottest indie, electro and rock music, courtesy of DJs Jared Allen and Sean Watson, and a rotating list of guest DJs.

name: Steppers Tuesdays

description: The DJ spins popular tracks.

description: DJ Flattop spins music.

location: 2515 N. Scottsdale Road, Suite 12 Scottsdale, AZ, 85257

name: Forbidden
description: This dance club includes two dance floors and multiple DJs.

name: '80s Dance Party
description: Every Saturday night, this Scottsdale nightclub offers some of the biggest dance hits of the 1980s, with a couple of modern Top 40 hits thrown in for good measure by DJ Gregg.

price: $8 for ages 18 to 21, no cover for 21-and-older
description: For those 18-and-older, the Fresh Friday dance party features a Top 40 Video Remix Party with DJ Sterling or DJ Mic Mixxer. And each week offers a different twist, with the second Friday of each month featuring a FindFred.com and BoyCrush.com party, on third Fridays the Dynamite Divas Drag Show with Mikaila Kay, and the the last Friday of each month the Glow Party with DJ Mic Mixxers. 21-and-older partiers can also get a red cup for $15, with penny refills all night on a list of popular cocktails.

name: Salsa Night

description: This dance club/lounge offers signature drinks, champagne, beer and wine. Specialty martinis include the Devil's Martini, made with Tanqueray gin, and the French Devil with Skyy vodka, pineapple liqueur, Chambord and pineapple juice. Two-for-one cocktail specials offered every Friday and Saturday.

With the mingling of the industry crowd and common folk, this is a new way for a DJ-in-training to try out for the big time. If the crowd digs it, then a full time gig might be in the works. For age 21 and older.

name: Parsons Dance Company and East Village Opera
venue: Scottsdale Center for the Performing Arts
description: The dance troupe, Parsons Dance Company, and opera company East Village Opera, join forces for a production of "Remember Me," a modern retelling of the classic love triangle, with contemporary dance moves, live and recorded music, digital lighting, video projections and visual effects.

location: 7353 E. Indian School Road Scottsdale, AZ, 85251

description: Kick off the weekend party with Harlot Fridays at Hotel Theodore. DJ William Reed spins in the Red Bar while DJ Tricky T performs in the Midnight Room. Ladies are treated to $5 martinis all night.

Special events include Ladies' Night on Wednesdays with $4 drinks and $2 shots until 11 p.m. Get $2 drinks on the patio from 9-10 p.m. Fridays.

description: Listen to classical sounds and songs performed by Paradise Valley Community College's Classical Ensemble. In the Center for Performing Arts.

description: Hit this Scottsdale hotspot Friday nights to check out all six rooms and two levels of the club, while DJ Phlava spins the hottest hip-hop and R&B in the Main Room and DJ Dark Vader plays reggae in the ballroom.

venue: Scottsdale Center for the Performing Arts
description: The classical pianist performs selections from his new CD, "Out of My Hands," which includes music written by Tori Amos, Tears for Fears, Radiohead and classical composers Ravel and Chopin. He is the only classical pianist to ever receive a four-star review from Rolling Stone magazine.

name: Twist Thursdays
description: Myst opens its doors to the 18 and older crowd, with a rotating list of DJs spinning some of the hottest dance, hip-hip and R&B tunes in all the club's six rooms.

name: "Keyboard Conversations" with Jeffrey Siegel
venue: Scottsdale Center for the Performing Arts
description: In between selections, the pianist talks to the audience about the music. At this event, Siegel takes the audience on a tour of Paris, circa 1911, with pieces including Ravel's "Valses Nobles et Sentimentales" and Stravinsky's "Petrouchka." The show also features Keyboard in the Sky, a technological enhancement above the stage that enables the audience to see the pianist's hands as they move across the keyboard.

name: DJ Mikyl
description: This DJs brings the party when he's on deck spinning new and old hits every week.

name: "High Notes" (The Ballad of Downtown Jake)
description: Lois Roma-Deeley, winner of the Samuel T. Coleridge Literary Prize and Paradise Valley Community College faculty member, is the author of three collections of poetry including "High Notes." The book forms the basis of a jazz opera she is writing with composer and Paradise Valley Community College faculty member Christopher Scinto. The staged reading of the jazz opera is performed by four singers and a chamber ensemble.

name: Pinky Ring
description: This Wednesday night dance party may have left its downtown Phoenix home for the Old Town scene, but DJs Benjamin Cutswell, Death to the Throne and Bigie are still spinning their mix of electro, hip-hop and rock.

name: Nobuyuki Tsujii
venue: Scottsdale Center for the Performing Arts
description: Born blind in 1988, Tsujii learned to play "Jingle Bells" on a toy piano at age 2 after hearing his mother hum the tune. He began his formal training at 4. He debuted with the Century Orchestra Osaka at 10 and has been performing for audiences ever since.

name: CTRL+ALT+DEL
description: DJs Emile, Tricky T and Radar hit the decks Wednesdays at this Tempe club, spinning across six turntables to create soundscapes of hip-hop, drum and bass, dubstep, electro, and glitch.

location: 6947 E. McDonald Drive Paradise Valley, AZ, 85253
name: "Crossing Paths"
description: The Sonoran Desert Chorale closes out its season with this spirited concert, which features music the group will perform on their upcoming annual international tour, which includes stops in Austria, Hungary and Slovenia.

name: GALLERY BLU re:DEF Hip Hop Night
description: Every Tuesday night, this Tempe bar hosts a slew of local and national DJs spinning some of the hottest hip-hop tracks. Resident DJs Emgee and Cre One hit the decks, along with special guests each week.

name: Classical Ensembles Concert
description: Hear music classics performed by Paradise Valley Community College's classical-music ensemble featuring choir, flute ensemble, orchestra, percussion and piano. This performance is held in the college's Center for Performing Arts.

location: 1423 S. Country Club Drive Mesa, AZ, 85210
name: DJ Sissko
description: DJ Sissko plays electro house/garage/trance/progressive tunes and appears weekly along with different guest DJs at Goat's Head Saloon. The Mesa bar hosts ongoing karaoke nights, poker tournaments, darts and open-mike nights. Look for drink specials and grub like sliders, nachos, burgers and sandwiches.

name: Weekend Musical Delights
description: Violinist Dimitri Lazarescu performs on electric and acoustic violins.

name: Swing Night
description: A swing lesson, followed by a dance at 8 p.m. For ages 21 and older.

name: Club Nights
description: Every Friday and Saturday night, this central Phoenix club hosts a rockin' dance night, featuring Latin, old school and hip-hop tracks courtesy of DJ Money. The night also features $4 shot specials and drink specials that include $2 Bud Lights, $3 well drinks and $3 select draft beers.

name: Riders in the Sky
description: This Grammy Award-winning country quartet infuses their shows with humor and Western wit. Performing for more than 30 years, they were the first exclusively Western music artists to join the Grand Ole Opry radio show.

name: Ricky Skaggs and Kentucky Thunder
description: The country superstar and winner of multiple music awards performs with his band. Skaggs first performed on stage at age 6, playing mandolin with bluegrass legend, Bill Monroe. In the 1990s and 2000s, Skaggs has strived to incorporate that bluegrass sound into his country offerings.

name: Steve Wariner
description: The country musician performs music that spans his career, which began as a teenager, playing bass and singing at 17. He went on to release 18 studio albums and win several Grammy Awards. In 2003, he started his own record label called Selectone Records.

name: The Lennon Sisters
description: The sisters, known for their flawless harmonies, have been performing for nearly 50 years, since they began on the "Lawrence Welk" show.

name: Clay Aiken
description: This North Carolina pop singer first arrived on the national scene on the second season of "American Idol." Although he lost to Ruben Studdard, Aiken established a loyal fan base from the show. His debut album, 2003's "Measure of a Man" hit No. 1 on the Billboard 100 charts and went multiplatinum. His success has continued over the years, and he released his latest album, "Tried and True," in 2010.

name: The Diamonds
description: It's been more than 50 years since the release of the Diamonds' big hit, "Little Darlin'." Audience members will go back in time when the Diamonds perform some of their biggest hits during two shows at Valle Del Oro. Show times are 4 and 7:30 p.m.

name: The Persuasions
description: This a cappella group began singing together in Brooklyn in 1961, and the band has released 18 albums, recording and performing with a number of top artists, including Liza Minnelli, Bette Midler, Stevie Wonder, Lou Reed, Van Morrison, Paul Simon and B.B. King.

name: Frank Sinatra Jr.
description: The singer, songwriter and conductor performs with a 20-piece orchestra. Born in 1944, the son of legendary crooner Frank Sinatra started performing in his early teens, and by 1968, he had performed in 47 states and 30 countries and had made guest appearances on several television shows.

name: Lady Gaga
description: This New York City superstar returns to the Valley. Her July concert drew more than 14,000 fans. Lady Gaga has dominated the pop universe for the past two years with her over-the-top fashion sense, elaborate performances and outspoken politics and has ruled the charts with hits such as Just Dance" and "Poker Face," "LoveGame," "Paparazzi," "Bad Romance," "Telephone" and "Alejandro." She released her second album, "The Fame Monster," in 2009.

name: Betty Buckley
venue: Scottsdale Center for the Performing Arts
description: The actress and singer is fresh from the off-Broadway production "White Lies." She performs "Broadway by Request," a selection of show tunes hand-picked by the audience and delivered in a candid, storytelling style.

name: The Manhattan Transfer
venue: Scottsdale Center for the Performing Arts
description: The long-running group performs selections from their recent CD, "The Chick Corea Songbook," along with some bebop, swing, standards and doo-wop.

name: Dan Zanes and Friends
venue: Scottsdale Center for the Performing Arts
description: The former singer of the roots-rock band the Del Fuegos heads up this band, which performs fun, family oriented music that not only includes the traditional rock instruments - guitar, bass and drums - but others, such as the tuba, accordion, pump organ, djembe and saw.

location: Hotel Theodore 7353 E. Indian School Road Scottsdale, AZ, 85251
name: Javier Garcia Tuesday Nights
description: Tuesday nights just got a lot more chill. Stop by to hear the tunes of local musician Javier Garcia as he performs popular pop/rock covers such as Wonderwall and Dead or Alive. Make your taste buds feel good, too, with drinks specials like half-price wine, beer and well martinis. Age 21 and older.

location: 7303 E. Indian School Road Scottsdale, AZ, 85251
name: Carumba Live!
description: Kick back and chill out with some of The Valley's best young musicians playing your favorite covers and their own songs in the Margarita Bar, an intimate setting with a casual, friendly and fun vibe. While enjoying the music, quench your thirst with a hand-poured margarita and dine on the Nuevo Mexican food.

name: The Salvation Showdown
description: Hosted by Paisley Yankolovich with various artists each week.

name: Joey D. and Pat Starke
description: The musicians perform oldies.

description: The music series is from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m. each Thursday at the Metro Stage in Stetson Plaza. Concerts spotlight local pop, rock and jazz bands. This series is presented by the Scottsdale Arts District in conjunction with the Scottsdale Gallery Association and the City of Scottsdale.

name: Jack Wells and Friends
description: Ragtime and jazz music.

name: Showstoppers Live
description: 7 and 9 p.m. Wednesday-Saturday; 7 p.m. Sunday and Tuesday. Hear some of the greatest sounds in pop music, featuring the songs of the Temptations, Elvis, Tina Turner, the Four Tops and Madonna.

location: 8852 E. Pinnacle Peak Road Scottsdale, AZ, 85255

description: The pianist performs cover songs in the piano bar.

name: A Boy Named Sioux
description: Led by Rob Toner, this Tempe band blends outlaw country with elements of Southern rock and Southwestern twists, resulting in a sound somewhere between Waylon Jennings and Roger Clyne. The group performs tunes from their debut EP, "The Next Big Thing."

name: Best of Phoenix Open Mic hosted by Troy
description: Monday nights, the Yucca is the best place to hear local bands and singer-songwriters, as the bar hosts this weekly open-mike night.

description: This Western-themed bar has wood-paneled walls, a saloon mural and a checkered dance floor. Take advantage of free line-dancing lessons at 7 p.m. Thursdays or compete in Texas Hold'em tournaments Wednesdays. Karaoke starts at 8 p.m. Sundays. On the weekends, you may see a few Stetsons, but the DJ keeps it interesting by mixing two-step with hip-hop.

name: Silver Pony
description: Whether its the Saguaro Sunset Band, the Bullet Band or Sidewinder, be prepared to kick back in a twangy glory and hear both current and classic country sounds at the Silver Pony. Happy hour is from 6-10 a.m. and 4-7 p.m. Monday through Friday and features 25-cent specials. Karaoke is held Thursday and Sunday nights.

name: Peso Dollar Band
description: Formed in the early 1950's, Peso Dollar has performed with various members on stage with Roy Rogers, Gene Autry, Jerry Lee Lewis, Vince Gill and Don Henly among others. Now, you can catch the band, after over 50 years while grabbing a bite to eat. Also pick up their most current album, Gypsy Soul, for $15.

description: Rock-U Thursdays features food and drink specials along with live bands. Hear local cover bands perform rock and country tunes while enjoying half off appetizers, $2 Widmer Hefeweizen, $3 Captain Morgan spiced rum and $5 Vodka Red Bulls. Become a friend of Cadillac Ranch on facebook to win entry to a VIP party with penny cocktails from 9–10:30 p.m.

name: Tom Ryan's
description: Drink, dance and listen to live music starting at 9:15 p.m. Thursday-Saturday.

name: DeLon
description: A country-music performance.

description: The good people at Coyote Alley certainly know how to live it up country-style. The weekends are reserved for live music with acts such as Adam McGraw and his Poison Whiskey Band and Western Fusion both regularly filling the music slots. You'll also find karaoke, darts and pool tables. With a Monday special of mojitos and martinis, Coyote Alley is more than just a country bar.

location: 6895 E. Cave Creek Road Cave Creek, AZ, 85331
name: Rondavous Acoustic
description: The five-piece country/Southern rock band breaks down for an acoustic performance singing originals and cover songs from artists such as George Strait, Aretha Franklin and Shania Twain.

location: 6811 E. Cave Creek Road Cave Creek, AZ, 85331
name: Buffalo Chip Saloon and Steakhouse
description: This Western saloon and steak house offers dancing, live music, karaoke, mesquite-smoked cowboy chow and happy-hour specials from 2-6 p.m. Monday-Friday.

location: 6185 W. Hunt Highway Queen Creek, AZ, 85242
name: San Tan Flat
description: Though not related, San Tan Flat resembles Greasewood Flat in concept. The bar is open-air with picnic tables forming a half-moon around a small stage. San Tan Flat is newer, bigger and fancier than the historic Greasewood Flat. The barstools at San Tan Flat are leather saddles, which may be the closest you’ll ever come to the open range. San Tan Flat also is great for families; kids can run around, dance and roast marshmallows while mom and dad enjoy a beer.

name: Great Big Sea
description: This Canadian folk-rock band from Newfoundland and Labrador are best known for their high-energy rock interpretations of traditional Newfoundland folk songs. The band performs a number of sea shanties, which draw from the island's 500-year-old history. The group's latest album, 2010's "Safe Upon the Shore," debuted at No. 2 on the on the Canadian Albums Charts.

name: Septeto Nacional De Cuba
description: This Cuban group has been performing for more then 80 years, playing the music of Ignacio Piñeiro and traditional Cuban Son music to audiences worldwide.

description: Led by Dubliner Liam Mackey, this Phoenix band plays a rowdy blend of rock and Celtic folk songs, creating a sound that crosses the humor of Barenaked Ladies with the music of the Pogues. Coyote Alley

name: "Agave on the Rocks"
description: Agave on the Rocks returns to the Desert Botanical Garden, offering Southwestern and Mexican fare prepared by renowned Valley chefs, paired with specialty margaritas and an eclectic mix of Latin-inspired music. This year's event features local favorites Roger Clyne and P.H. Naffah of Roger Clyne and the Peacemakers performing an acoustic set from their upcoming album, “Unida Cantina." Visitors can also meet the musicians and purchase a bottle of Clyne’s Mexican Moonshine Tequila. Additional music provided by local bands Bata Ire, Locura and Jaleo Salsa. A 21-and-older show.

name: "Man in Black: The Legend of Johnny Cash"
description: Robert Shaw and the Lonely Street Band celebrate what would have been Johnny Cash’s 79th birthday with this multi-media tribute show, featuring songs such as "Folsom Prison Blues,""I Walk the Line,""Ring of Fire," and "A Boy Named Sue." Dinner begins at 5:30 p.m. both nights, and at noon for the Saturday matinée.

name: Aaron Lewis
description: As the lead singer of the rock band Staind, this Massachusetts singer-songwriter landed hit singles such as "It's Been Awhile" and "Outside," along with four platinum albums. In recent years, Lewis has moved in a country-rock direction, and arrives in support of his debut solo EP, this year's "Town Line."

name: Country Thunder
description: Nashville superstars Toby Keith and Martina McBride headline two nights of this year's edition of "Country Thunder." Rising country star Jason Aldean headlines April 8, and veteran country-rock band Sawyer Brown kicks the festival off April 7. See website for a complete lineup of this year's featured musicians and bands.

name: Loretta Lynn
description: This Kentucky-born country music legend has landed 16 No. 1 country hits during her decadeslong career and influenced a generation of musicians. Known for songs such as "Don't Come Home A' Drinkin' (With Lovin' on Your Mind)," "Fist City" and "Woman of the World (Leave My World Alone)," Lynn also wrote a 1976 autobiography,"Coal Miner's Daughter," which was made into the 1980 Academy Award-winning film of the same name, starring Sissy Spacek and Tommy Lee Jones. In 2004, Lynn teamed with Jack White of the White Stripes for her Grammy Award-winning album "Van Lear Rose," which reached No. 2 on the Billboard Top Country Albums chart. The tribute album "Coal Miner's Daughter: A Tribute to Loretta Lynn" was released in 2010, featuring performances by top artists such as Gretchen Wilson, Alan Jackson, Paramore, the White Stripes, Kid Rock and Lucinda Williams.

location: 2000 E. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Gradymusic
description: Scottsdale-based keyboardist Grady Soiné performs his easy-listening tunes, including songs from his latest album, 2001's "Beautiful." Performing on the Barnes and Noble Fountain Stage.

location: 3301 S. Goldfield Road Apache Junction, AZ, 85219
name: Variety Show
description: This variety showcase features musical talent from Las Vegas and entertainers from the Southwest. Complimentary refreshments are served. Presented by M&M Productions.

name: Psychedelic Mooj
description: This Chandler band plays a mix of rock, funk, soul, jazz and psychedelic blues. The group recently released its latest album, "Analog Soup." Rock bands Fat Tree and Keeping Shay also perform.

location: 6033 E. Cave Creek Road Cave Creek, AZ, 85331
name: Ronny Cox
venue: Cave Creek Coffee Co. and Wine Purveyors
description: This singer-songwriter and actor made his film debut in the 1972 film "Deliverance," playing guitar in the film's memorable "Dueling Banjos" tune. As an actor, he's appeared in films such as "Beverly Hills Cop," "Total Recall" and more, and he released his latest album, "Songs ... With Repercussions," in 2008.

location: 80 W. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Arizona CityFest with Luis Palau
description: This two-day festival features the preaching of renowned Christian evangelist Luis Palau, musical performances from the Band Perry, Mat Kearney, Skillet, Israel Houghton, Toby Mac, Contagious, Marisol and Phil Wickham. Other events include a Family Fun Zone featuring the Veggietales, and an action sports demo area, with bmx, fmx and skateboarding riders.

name: Laura Hull
description: This New Jersey jazz singer lends her sultry and expressive vocals to an extensive repertoire of popular songs, jazz standards and original tunes. Hull performs songs from her latest album, 2008's "Take Me Home." An 18-and-older show.

name: "The Motown Spectacular Show"
description: Hosted by comedian Jimmie "J.J." Walker, this tribute to Motown features performances of classic hits by the Temptations, the Supremes, Smokey Robinson, the Four Tops, Marvin Gaye, Stevie Wonder, the Marvelettes and more.

name: "Jazz It Up for Literacy" with Dennis Rowland and the Extreme Decibel Big Band
description: Herberger Theater Performing and Broadcast Arts Hall of Fame singer Dennis Rowland, former lead singer for the Count Basie Orchestra, performs jazz standards and blues tunes with the Valley's Extreme Decibel Big Band. The evening includes an hors d'oeuvres reception and silent auction. Proceeds benefit the Arizona Literacy & Learning Center, which helps Arizonans with reading problems, dyslexia, auditory difficulties and learning disabilities. An 18-and-older event.

name: Sunday A’Fair
venue: Scottsdale Center for the Performing Arts
description: This free concert features local favorites Cold Shott and the Hurricane Horns, playing their high-energy R&B and blues tunes. The afternoon also features local band Desert Gumbo's mix of R&B, zydeco, swing, calypso, reggae, delta blues and rock.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Bad News Blues Band
description: This Tucson five-piece plays a groovy blend of blues, funk and rock, with a powerful horn sound and a slinky rhythm section. The band has released several albums, include 2008's "Live at Hot Licks" and 2004's "Still Cadillacin.'”

name: Sunday A’Fair
venue: Scottsdale Center for the Performing Arts
description: This final installment of this Sunday-afternoon music series, this concert features the music of jazz group Larry Redhouse Trio, playing songs from their latest album, "Spirit Progression." the show also features the Living Traditions Dance Troupe, presenting a celebration of Native American culture, music and dance.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Cold Shott and the Hurricane Horns
description: This eight-piece Arizona R&B band has been performing together for more than 20 years, gaining a reputation for its funky, high-energy stage shows. The group released a live album, "If You Got the Blues...," in 2003.

location: JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort and Spa 5350 E. Marriott Drive Phoenix, AZ, 85054
name: Desert Ridge Jazz Festival
description: Day 1 performers are Richard Elliott and Norman Brown, Jonathan Butler, Eric Dairus, Maysa, Euge Groove, Mindi Abair and Turning Point. Day 2 offers Guitars & Saxes with Jeff Golub, Gerald Albright and Kirk Whalum, Gentlemen of the Night with Marion Meadows, Paul Taylor and Warren Hill, Steve Cole, Nick Colionne, Jeff Kashiwa and Jackiem Joyner, Jessy J and Dominic Amato.

name: Tempe Community Chorus: "The Joint is Jumping"
description: The Tempe Community Chorus performs an upbeat concert of jazz tunes, Broadway hits and gospel selections.

name: Music on Main Concert Series: G Force
description: This Phoenix group performs a hot mix of R&B classics and modern hits, adding in elements of Latin jazz and funk.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Cold Shott and the Hurricane Horns
description: This eight-piece Arizona R&B band has been performing together for more than 20 years, gaining a reputation for its funky, high-energy stage shows. The group released a live album, "If You Got the Blues...," in 2003.

name: Music in the Garden: Dennis Rowland
description: Dennis Rowland grew up in Detroit, surrounded by blues and R&B. In 1977 he became the voice of the Count Basie Orchestra, following in the footsteps of his idol, Joe Williams. Rowland is a member of the Herberger Theater Performing and Broadcast Arts Hall of Fame. He recently released his latest album, "Now Dig This." This popular event also features a chef-attended food station featuring weekly specials for an additional charge, along with a cash bar. A 21-and-older event.

name: Jazz on the Promenade Series: Cold Shott and the Hurricane Horns
description: This eight-piece Arizona R&B band has been performing together for more than 20 years, gaining a reputation for funky, high-energy stage shows. The group released a live album, "If You Got the Blues...," in 2003. This event also features wine tastings and specialty food sampling for an extra charge, with proceeds going to the non-profit group City of Hope, which works to fight cancer, diabetes, HIV/AIDS and other life-threatening diseases.

name: Ken Waldman: Alaska's Fiddling Poet
description: Old-time fiddle music is paired with original poetry from storyteller, Ken Waldman.

location: 7000 E. Mayo Blvd., Suite 21 Phoenix, AZ, 85054
name: McDowell Mountain Music Festival
description: This annual music festival returns to the Compound Grill for the second year in a row, bringing a batch of indie favorites, jam bands and world music groups. This year's festival is headlined by hippie indie-folk rockers Edward Sharpe and the Magnetic Zeros and blues rockers Black Joe Lewis and the Honeybears. The lineup also includes performances by JJ Grey and Mofro, SOJA, Xavier Rudd and the Otis Taylor Band. Proceeds benefit Ear Candy, a non-profit music education organization, and Phoenix Day, an organization that works with early education programs.

name: Music in the Garden: Hot Birds and the Chili Sauce
description: This 11-piece Phoenix band performs its rare groove-funk and soul sound, inspired by legends such as Sam & Dave and Wilson Pickett. The band has shared the stage with Gil Scott-Heron, Robert Randolph and Orgone, and released its debut EP, “Live at the Sail Inn,” in 2010. This popular event also features a chef-attended food station featuring weekly specials for an additional charge, along with a cash bar. A 21-and-older event.

name: Bruno Mars/Janelle Monáe
description: Playing as part of their co-headlining tour, Hooligans in Wondaland, these soulful pop stars arrive in support of their hit debut albums. Los Angeles singer-songwriter Bruno Mars broke out after lending his vocals to "Billionaire" by Travie McCoy, before releasing his solo debut, 2010's "Doo-Wops & Hooligans." The album debuted at No. 3 on the Billboard 200 charts, and the lead single, "Just the Way You Are," topped the Billboard Hot 100 for four consecutive weeks. Combing elements of classic funk and soul, Kansas City, Mo., singer-songwriter Janelle Monáe released her debut album, "The ArchAndroid (Suites II and III)," in 2010, earning a Grammy nomination for best contemporary R&B album. Los Angeles soul band Mayer Hawthorne and the County open this all-ages show.

name: The Rhythm Ramblers
description: This 18-piece Sun City big band performs classic hits from the big band era, joined by singers Marge Nelson and Kent Parry. This dance is held the first Tuesday of each month.

location: 16844 N. Arrowhead Fountains Center Drive Peoria, AZ, 85382
name: ABBAFab
description: Paying tribute to Sweden's biggest musical export and one of the the best-selling pop acts in history, this ABBA tribute show offers a string of hit tracks such as "Waterloo," "Fernando," ""Take a Chance on Me," "Mamma Mia" and "Dancing Queen." Performances at 5:30 and 8 p.m. Friday and Saturday.

location: 6640 S. Kings Ranch Road Gold Canyon, AZ, 85218
name: Phoenix Vocal Jazz
description: The six voices of Phoenix Vocal Jazz deliver exciting performances of jazz standards with tight harmonies and dramatic flair, in the style of groups such as the Manhattan Transfer. The group performs songs from its album of jazz standards, "Timeless."

name: Lady Gaga Monster Ball After-Party with Lady Stardust
description: Following the Lady Gaga concert at US Airways Center, head down the street to Bar Smith for this after-party, featuring Lady Stardust, the official Monster Ball DJ and Gaga collaborator. The event also features DJ sets by Robbie Rob, Bigie, Mane One, Austin Head, Pete Salaz, DJ Senbad, 2Tone Disco and Jonny Noir, along with live art and striptease performances.

location: 5040 W. Wild Horse Pass Blvd. Gila River Reservation, AZ, 85246
name: Mitzi Gaynor
description: This film legend has starred in films such as 1954's "There's No Business Like Show Business," 1957's " Les Girls" and 1958's "South Pacific." This multi-media show features Gaynor performing songs from her films, telling stories about her star-studded life and offering video footage of some of her greatest roles. (Photo courtesy of Wild Horse Pass Hotel & Casino)

name: "Lucky Break" Season 5
description: This "American Idol"-style singing competition offers Valley singers a shot at stardom. Singers perform for a panel of judges on the show, which is broadcast on Channel 5 (KPHO), competing for a cash prize of $10,000 and an opportunity to showcase their talents to top record executives. Auditions for the show are held at at 8 p.m. Wednesdays Jan. 26 to March 30. The show is broadcast at 11:35 p.m. Saturdays from Feb. 2 to June 2 See website for official rules. Registration required.

name: Manhattan Transfer
description: This celebrated vocal group arrives in celebration of its 40th anniversary, a career that has seen millions of album sales, multiple Grammy awards and sold-out international tours. The group released its latest album, "The Chick Corea Songbook," in 2009.

name: Janet Jackson
description: This pop icon returns to the Valley as part of her Number Ones, Up Close and Personal Tour, which features Jackson performing some of her biggest hits in more intimate venues, without the special effects of her previous tours. Sister to Michael Jackson, Janet Jackson has sold more than 100 million albums worldwide, scoring huge hits with songs such as "Nasty," "Rhythm Nation," "That's the Way Love Goes" and "All for You." Her 10th album, 2008's "Discipline," debuted at No. 1 on the U.S. Billboard 200 chart.

location: 7007 W. Happy Valley Road Peoria, AZ, 85383
name: Chris Tomlin
description: This American Dove Award-winning Christian singer-songwriter arrives behind his latest release, "And If Our God Is For Us ..."

name: Rod Stewart/Stevie Nicks
description: Rock and Roll Hall of Famers Rod Stewart and Stevie Nicks team up for a night of rock and roll hits, performing songs from throughout their long careers. A former member of Fleetwood Mac, Nicks has landed more than 40 Top 50 hits and sold more than 140 million albums. Know for his raspy singing style, Steward was ranked No. 17 on "The Billboard Hot 100 Top All-Time Artists," with more than 100 million records sold.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Yelle
description: This French electro-pop band has appeared at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival and are supporting Katy Perry on her California Dreams Tour. Yelle arrive in support of their sophomore album, 2011's "Safari Disco Club." New York's French Horn Rebellion open this all-ages show.

location: 5040 W. Wild Horse Pass Blvd. Gila River Reservation, AZ, 85246
name: The B-52s
description: Rooted in the sounds of New Wave and 1960s rock and roll, this Athens, Ga., band has scored hits with quirky singles such as "Rock Lobster," "Love Shack" and "Roam." The band released "Funplex" in 2008, its first original album in 16 years.

name: Arts in the Park Concert: Thaddeus Rose & Friends
Yanni
description: This New Age music legend returns to the Valley, performing songs from his highly anticipated new album, "Touch of Truth," his first album of original studio music in almost a decade. Yanni has sold more than 20 millions albums worldwide, scoring more than 35 platinum and gold albums. Known for his live shows, Yanni has performed at top venues around the world, including the Acropolis of Athens, the Taj Mahal, the Forbidden City in China and Royal Albert Hall in England.

name: Backstreet Boys/New Kids on the Block
description: With more than 200 million albums sold between them, boy-band legends the Backstreet Boys and the New Kids on the Block arrive together on their NKOTBSB Tour. The New Kids on the Block set the standard for boy-band success in the 1980s and '90s, winning over fans with hits such as "Step By Step," "Summertime" and "Hangin' Tough." The Backsteet Boys dominated the pop charts in the '90s and early 2000s with hits such as "I Want It That Way," "Larger Than Life" and "Just Want You to Know." The two bands perform together at this show, singing medleys of their combined greatest hits, as well as songs from their latest albums, 2008's "The Block" by the New Kids on the Block and the Backstreet Boys' 2009 release, "This Is Us."

name: Katy Perry
description: This pop superstar arrives in the Valley as part of her worldwide California Dreams tour. The California singer first hit the mainstream with her No. 1 2008 hit, "I Kissed a Girl." Perry's third album, 2010's "Teenage Dream," debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 chart and spawned the hit singles "California Gurls," "Teenage Dream" and "Firework." The album is also nominated for album of the year and best pop vocal album at the 53rd Grammy Awards.

location: 524 N. 92nd St. Salt River Reservation, AZ, 85256
name: Showstoppers Live
description: 7 and 9 p.m. Wednesday-Saturday; 7 p.m. Sunday and Tuesday. Hear some of the greatest sounds in pop music, featuring the songs of the Temptations, Elvis, Tina Turner, the Four Tops and Madonna.

name: Pete Pancrazi
description: This jazz guitarist has been playing in the Valley since the early 1990s and has been named "Jazz Guitar Player of the Year" by the AzJazz Magazine Readers' Poll. He'll perform songs from his four albums, including tunes from "Trio Songbook" and "Stand Alone." Performing on the AMC fountain stage.

name: Rock Lobster
description: Take a trip back to the 1980s Saturday nightswith this local retro party band, as it takes on everything from Billy Idol's "White Wedding" to Cyndi Lauper's "Girl's Just Want to Have Fun."

location: 16844 N. Arrowhead Fountains Center Drive Peoria, AZ, 85382
name: Take It to the Limit: A Tribute to the Eagles
description: This Phoenix band plays hits such as "Desperado," "Peaceful Easy Feeling," "Lyin' Eyes" and "Hotel California." Show times at 5 and 8 p.m.

name: Rockstar Wednesdays Live Music Showcase
description: Pre-chosen local bands perform in a live radio music showcase for Rockstar Wednesdays. All bands are welcome to interview and audition to perform. Drink specials offered all night long. Hosted by KWSS 106.7 Live Radio Show.

location: 2000 E. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Think Horses
description: This five-piece Scottsdale group plays a blend of music, incorporating elements of rock, jazz, rumba, Celtic funk and blues. Performing on the District stage.

location: 2000 E. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Just Jade
description: Guitarists Cory Fournier and Mara Hayes make up this local duo, performing the soulful acoustic tracks from their new album, “Fortunately Found." Performing on the Barnes and Noble fountain stage.

name: The Dames
description: This Phoenix all-girl power-punk trio performs song from their latest record, "Take a Number." Punk bands Casket Life, the Father Figures, Wirefeeder and the Smoky Mountain Skullbusters also perform at this 21-and-older show.

name: Peppermint James
description: Taking inspiration from the music of the Beatles, along with jazz, blues and reggae artists, these local rockers released their self-titled debut in 2008. The group has performed at the McDowell Mountain Music Festival, sharing the stage with the Jon Butler Trio, Blues Traveler and the Wailers. Performing on the District stage.

name: Wednesday Nights at Conspire
description: On Wednesday nights, this hip downtown Phoenix hangout plays hosts to an open mike night, which attracts many local poets, actors and musicians. Plus there's plenty of coffee and vegan donuts to go around.

location: Mill Avenue and University Drive Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Music On Mill
description: Musicians and performers of all sorts line the streets throughout the district giving visitors a variety of entertainment. Mill Avenue is where historic music venues such as Long Wong's, Gibson's and Edsel's Attic were located at one time that became the launchpads for bands such as the Gin Blossoms, the Refreshments, Dead Hot Workshop and Jimmy Eat World. Branded donation paint cans that are placed at each of their locations identify musicians scheduled to perform for Music on Mill.

name: Mythili Prakash
description: Specializing in Bharata Natyam, a classical dance of South India, Mythili Prakash has performed for audience around the world. Accompanied by Carnatic music, the South Indian classical form, Prakash performs the dynamic, emotional-filled art form.

name: Grupo Niche
description: This celebrated California salsa group was founded in 1978 in Bogotá, Colombia, and has long enjoyed great popularity throughout Latin America. The group released its latest album, "Alive," in 2005. A 21-and-older event.

name: Out to Lunch Series: JT’s Island Steel
description: The Mesa Arts Center's "Out to Lunch" concert series continues with performances by local steel drum group JT’s Island Steel, performing the classic Caribbean songs from their self-titled album.

location: 10424 N. Fort McDowell Road Fort McDowell Reservation, AZ, 85264
name: Ziggy Marley
description: The eldest son of reggae legend Bob Marley, this Jamaican singer-songwriter carries on his father's tradition, playing his own reggae tunes. Marley's 2006 album, "Love Is My Religion," hit No. 6 on the Billboard Top Reggae Albums charts and earned a Grammy award for Best Reggae Album. He released his latest album, "Family Time," in 2009.

name: American Sabor: Latinos in U.S. Popular Music
price: $15, $13 age 65 and older, $10 ages 6–17, free age 6 and younger
description: The first traveling exhibit to grace the Musical Instrument Museum in Phoenix, "American Sabor" showcases the influence and impact of Latinos in American popular music. The exhibit features artifacts, instruments, interactive audio and video displays, listening kiosks and films, as well as special musical events throughout the exhibits run. The exhibits covers everything from the the mambo, rhumba and cha-cha dance crazes of the 1950s to the East LA punk scene of the 1970s. It features instruments and other artifacts from performers such as Carlos Santana, Celia Cruz, Los Lobos, Linda Ronstadt, Tito Puente, Flaco Jiménez and more. Free with museum admission.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Sharon Van Etten
description: This Brooklyn signer-songwriter's debut album, 2009's" Because I Was In Love," showcased her mournful vocals and intimate playing. Van Etten appeared on the Antlers' critically acclaimed 2010 album "Hospice," and she released her sophomore effort, "Epic," in 2010. Canadian indie-rockers Little Scream opens this all-ages show.

location: 6602 E. Cave Creek Road Cave Creek, AZ, 85331
name: David Wilcox
description: The complex, thought-provoking folk tunes by this North Carolina singer-songwriter have made him a critical darling for more than two decades. Wilcox released his latest album, "Reverie," in 2010.

location: 5736 E. Rancho Mañana Blvd. Cave Creek, AZ, 85331
name: Ari Hest
description: Known for his dynamic guitar playing and introspective songs, this New York singer-songwriter returns to the Valley with music from his latest release, this year's "Sunset Over Hope Street."

location: 6033 E. Cave Creek Road Cave Creek, AZ, 85331
name: Gypsy Soul
venue: Cave Creek Coffee Co. and Wine Purveyors
description: This California-based Celtic/soul duo perform the gentle songs from their latest release, 2010's "Grace and Tranquility."

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Akron/Family
description: Arriving behind their latest album, this year's "S/T II:The Cosmic Birth and Journey of Shinju TNT," these Portland, Ore., indie rockers fill their folk-influenced songs with psychedelic and electronic elements, along with other experimental effects. Indie rock band Delicate Steve opens this 21-and-older show.

name: Music in the Garden: Leila Lopez
description: This Tucson singer-songwriter's finger-picked guitar style and poetic lyrics have earned her comparisons to Ani Difranco and Fiona Apple. Lopez recently took home the Tucson Area Music Award for best female vocalist and best songwriter for her new album, 2010's "Fault Lines." This popular event also features a chef-attended food station featuring weekly specials for an additional charge, along with a cash bar. A 21-and-older event.

name: Music on Main Concert Series: Sean Mireau and the Volcano Island Band
description: Wrapping up the concert series, this Phoenix steel drum group performs the laid-back music of Jimmy Buffett, Bob Marley and other Caribbean-flavored hits.

name: William Fitzsimmons
description: The gentle folk-rock tunes by this Illinois-based singer-songwriter have appeared on the TV series "Grey's Anatomy," "Brothers & Sisters," "Life of Ryan" and "One Tree Hill." Fitzsimmons released his latest album, "Derivatives," in 2010. Indie-rockers Slow Runners open this all-ages show.

name: Mariachi Los Rebeldes
description: Performing as part of the museum's "American Sabor: Latinos in U.S. Popular Music" exhibition, this Phoenix-based youth mariachi troupe brings energy and fun to the traditional Mexican music genre.

name: Balinese Gamelan Workshop
description: Held every first and third Thursday of the month, this workshop provides an introduction to the musical tradition of gamelan angklung from Bali, Indonesia. Workshop participants learn briefly about Balinese music and culture, watch video samples of Balinese gamelan ensembles, learn proper etiquette and respect for the instruments and spend one hour in hands-on learning to play the gamelan as a group. Each class session is the same, so visitors need only to sign up for one class.

location: 10455 E. Pinnacle Peak Parkway Scottsdale, AZ, 85255
name: Mosaico
description: This Arizona flamenco group performs original music inspired by the sounds of Spain, Latin America and the Caribbean. Incorporating guitar, bass, flute, violin, piano and percussion, the group adds a taste of the Southwest to their performance.

name: "Spring is in the Air!"
venue: Ethington Theatre at Grand Canyon University
description: The Grand Canyon University music department presents this free concert, featuring the GCU choral ensembles and student and faculty soloists in an eclectic evening of vocal music dedicated to the season of spring.

name: Symphony Connections
description: Featuring 25 members of the Phoenix Symphony’s string section under the direction of assistant conductor Benjamin Rous, this free performance is meant to be engaging and entertaining. Rous explains the history and significance of each piece of music, and the ensemble performs the complete Simple Symphony by Benjamin Britten, along with works by Jean Sibelius, Tchaikovsky and Béla Bartók. Performance held in the Bulpitt Auditorium.

name: Out to Lunch Series: Scott Schaefer and Marina Miyoshi
description: Flutist Scott Schaefer and pianist Marina Miyoshi perform their New Age jazz tunes, playing as part of the Mesa Art Center's free "Out to Lunch" series. The duo perform the tranquil songs from their latest album, 2010's "Under One Sky."

location: 3900 E. Stanford Drive Paradise Valley, AZ, 85253
name: Scottsdale Musical Arts: "The Passion According to St. John"
description: The Scottsdale Choral Artists and Scottsdale Arts Chamber Orchestra presents this performance of J.S. Bach's "The Passion According to St. John."

name: Trio Sonnerie featuring Monica Huggett
description: The Trio Sonnerie is one of the most highly regarded chamber groups in Europe. Featuring violin, viola da gamba and harpsichord, the group preforms a range of Baroque pieces, joined by violinist Monica Huggett.

name: Arizona Young Artists’ Competition
description: Some of the top young singers, dancers and actors from around Arizona compete for the top prize at this 12th annual event. The show features performers ages 15-18. The top winner in each category takes home $1,000, and the audience can choose its favorite for the People's Choice award.

location: Scottsdale Civic Center Mall 3939 N. Drinkwater Blvd. Scottsdale, AZ, 85251
name: Opera in the Park: "La bohème"
description: Arizona Opera and Scottsdale Center for the Performing Arts present a free outdoor screening of Arizona Opera’s production of Puccini’s "La bohème," filmed live in 2010 at Symphony Hall in Phoenix. Set in 19th-century Paris, the beloved opera tells the story of the beautiful and frail seamstress Mimi and the poet Rodolfo. Low-sitting lawn chairs, pillows and blankets are welcome at the screening. Picnic food and beverages, including beer and wine, are available for sale.

location: Viad Tower 1850 N. Central Ave. Phoenix, AZ, 85004
name: Canyon Echoes: "A Hot Night at the Opera"
description: Canyon Echoes, the 20-man sub-ensemble of the Phoenix Metropolitan Men's Chorus, presents "A Hot Night at the Opera," which explores a fantasy world where it is the norm to have a same-sex marriage and heterosexuality is frowned upon. The story is told through music, featuring songs from "The Phantom of the Opera," a mock-opera by the rock band Queen, along with opera choruses and arias by Verdi, Mozart, Wagner, and Gilbert and Sullivan. The night also features songs from "Carmen" and Verdi's classic "Anvil Chorus."

name: King of Glory Concert Series: Phoenix Vocal Jazz and MCC Jazz Groups
description: Accompanied by the MCC Jazz Groups, the six voices of Phoenix Vocal Jazz deliver exciting performances of jazz standards with tight harmonies and dramatic flair, in the style of groups such as the Manhattan Transfer. The group performs songs from its album of jazz standards, "Timeless."

name: Scottsdale Musical Arts: "The Passion According to St. John"
venue: La Casa De Cristo Lutheran Church
description: The Scottsdale Choral Artists and Scottsdale Arts Chamber Orchestra present this performance of J.S. Bach's "The Passion According to St. John."

name: Chandler Symphony Orchestra Concert
description: The Chandler Symphony Orchestra joins the national Orchestras Feeding America movement, seeking non-perishable food donations to benefit the Chandler Food Bank and Matthew's Food Crossing. The orchestra performs music by Mikhail Glinka, Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov, Hector Berlioz, Richard Strauss and Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky.

name: Arizona Winds Concert Band
description: The Arizona Winds Concert Band welcomes the spring with this lively concert, featuring "La Belle Helene," William Walton’s "Crown Imperial," "Yankee Doodlin" and "American Overture for Band."

location: 8050 E. Mountain View Road Scottsdale, AZ, 85258
name: "Meet the Musicians"
description: The Phoenix Symphony Allegro host this free event, which lets visitors meet members of the Phoenix Symphony and hear them play and discuss their instruments. This month's edition features Symphony harpist Paula Provo. Other "Meet the Musicians" events will be held at the Mountain View Presbyterian Church on April 25.

name: MIM Wednesday Morning Interludes Series: ASU Contemporary Percussion Ensemble
description: Twenty-seven musicians from the School of Music of Arizona State University perform Stephen Ridley’s new "Symphony for Percussion."

name: Arizona Chamber Orchestra: Gershwin's "Porgy and Bess"
description: The Arizona Chamber Orchestra performs selections from one of America’s most beloved operas, George Gershwin's "Porgy and Bess," featuring acclaimed harmonica virtuoso Miroslav Boži. The evening also features Maurice Ravel's Sonata for Violin and Piano and Benjamin Britten's "Simple Symphony."

name: Music in the Garden: Domingo DeGrazia
description: This Arizona native combines his flamenco guitar work with vibrant Latin, salsa and rock drum beats. He released his solo guitar album, "San Carlos," in 2007 and worked with violinist Beth Daunis on the 2010 record "The Bluest Sky." This popular event also features a chef-attended food station featuring weekly specials for an additional charge, along with a cash bar. A 21-and-older event.

name: Arizona Chamber Orchestra: Selections from Gershwin's "Porgy and Bess"
description: The Arizona Chamber Orchestra wraps up their inaugural season at MIM with selections from one of America’s most beloved operas, George Gershwin's "Porgy and Bess," featuring acclaimed harmonica virtuoso Miroslav Boži. The evening also features Maurice Ravel's Sonata for Violin and Piano and Benjamin Britten's "Simple Symphony."

location: 700 W. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Arizona Chamber Orchestra: Gershwin's "Porgy and Bess"
description: The Arizona Chamber Orchestra performs selections from one of America’s most beloved operas, George Gershwin's "Porgy and Bess," featuring acclaimed harmonica virtuoso Miroslav Boži. The evening also features Maurice Ravel's Sonata for Violin and Piano and Benjamin Britten's "Simple Symphony."

name: KlezFest Concert: Klezmer Company Orchestra Presents "Beyond the Tribes"
description: The Klezmer Company Orchestra performs world Jewish music from its award-winning album, "Beyond the Tribes." Influenced by Latin, Mediterranean and American sounds, the record took home the awards for "Best Klezmer Album" and "Best Klezmer Song" for 2009 from Just Plain Folks, the world's largest independent music organization.

name: Solemn Evensong
description: The Cathedral Choir performs Solemn Evensong in celebration of Mothering Sunday. Solemn Evensong is a long-standing tradition in the Anglican church. The performance is followed by a reception in the Olney Gallery.

location: 6947 E. McDonald Drive Paradise Valley, AZ, 85253
name: Charles Small and His Trombone Choir
description: New York City trombonist Charles Small performs a mix of pops and classical music, arranged for trombone choir. The concert includes several George Gershwin pieces, along with selections from Giacomo Puccini's "La Boheme" and Bach's "Air from Suite No. 3 in D Major."

name: KlezFest Family: Klez4Kidz "Mendel's Accordion"
description: This multimedia presentation features the award-winning children's book "Mendel's Accordion" by Heidi Smith Hyde, accompanied by the Klezmer Company Orchestra. The performance features a dramatic reading, live music and projected illustrations from the book.

location: 700 W. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: "The European Connection"
description: The Tempe Symphonic Wind Ensemble performs classic wind selections from a number of European composers, including Gustav Holst, Camille Saint-Saëns, Benjamin Britten and Vasily Kalinnikov.

name: "Enchantment": A Spring Concert by Robin Miller
venue: New Vision Center for Spiritual Living
description: This acclaimed Sedona new-age, multi-instrumentalist performs the peaceful songs from his latest release, "Sedona Nights."

name: San Tan Chorale: "The 5th Year Flashback Concert"
description: The San Tan Chorale celebrates its fifth anniversary with this concert, featuring some of the chorale's favorite songs, ranging from classical works by Bach to show tunes by Gilbert and Sullivan. Non-perishable food donations are accepted to benefit local food pantries.

name: "Abduction from the Seraglio"
description: The Arizona Opera presents Mozart's German masterpiece of stolen love. The wild three-act opera tells the story of a young man whose true love is kidnapped by pirates and sold to the Pasha Selim. After trying to save her from the sultan, the lovers are captured, and a deadly secret is revealed. This is the first Arizona staging of this opera, which is sung in German with English supertitles.

name: King of Glory Concert Series: The Estrella Saxophone Consort
description: This ensemble features four saxophonists from Arizona State University, performing an innovative mix of chamber music and other genres.

name: Scottsdale Musical Arts: "Concerto Winners and Berlioz"
venue: La Casa De Cristo Lutheran Church
description: This concert features a performance of "Symphonie Fantastique" by Hector Berlioz, as well as performances by Scottsdale Musical Arts' Young Artists Concerto Competition winners.

location: 13459 W. Stardust Blvd. Sun City West, AZ, 85375
name: Sonoran Sounds Women's Chorale
description: The Sonoran Sounds Women's Chorale performs, featuring songs such as "Three Little Maids from School," a gospel rendition of "Go Where I Send Thee" and "Song For The Unsung Hero." The chorale is under the direction of Clarence Doornbos with piano accompaniment by Elaine Runkel.

location: 6640 S. Kings Ranch Road Gold Canyon, AZ, 85218
name: San Tan Chorale: "The 5th Year Flashback Concert"
description: The San Tan Chorale celebrates its fifth anniversary with this concert, featuring some of the Chorale's favorite songs, ranging from classical works by Bach to show tunes by Gilbert and Sullivan. Non-perishable food donations accepted to benefit local food pantries.

name: Central Arizona College Community Wind Ensemble Spring Concert
venue: Central Arizona College Signal Peak Campus
description: The 50-plus member Central Arizona College Community Wind Ensemble performs a range of concert band, well as lighter works.

location: 700 W. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Arizona Wind Symphony Concert
description: The Arizona Wind Symphony performs a wide variety of music, including marches, Broadway tunes, film themes, overtures, dances and contemporary symphonic wind music. The concert features a special honors performance by winners of the Small Ensemble Contest.

location: 8050 E. Mountain View Road Scottsdale, AZ, 85258
name: "Meet the Musicians"
description: The Phoenix Symphony Allegro host this free event, which lets visitors meet members of the Phoenix Symphony and hear them play and discuss their instruments. This final edition features Symphony violist Mark Deatherage.

name: MIM Wednesday Morning Interludes Series: Lynn Aspnes and Elizabeth Buck
description: Arizona State University faculty members Elizabeth Buck and Lynne Aspnes present "World Music for Flute and Harp," featuring the music of Claude-Achille Debussy, Marjan Mozetich and Tôru Takemitsu.

name: The Met: Live in HD Series: "Die Walküre"
The Met: Live in HD Series "Die Walküre"
Josh Groban
description: This celebrated, multiplatinum singer arrives in the Valley as part of his Straight to You Tour. Combining elements of operatic pop and pop rock, Groban's clear tenor voice and emotional songs have earned him a worldwide following, selling more than 24 million albums worldwide. Groban's most recent album, 2010's "Illuminations," debuted No. 4 on the Billboard 200 and has gone platinum in the U.S. and Canada.

location: 17300 N. Sun Village Parkway Surprise, AZ, 85374
name: Nicole Pesce
description: This celebrated Phoenix pianist spent many years in residence at the central Phoenix restaurant My Florist and the Ritz Carton Hotel, winning over diners with her virtuosic playing. With more than 500 songs committed to memory, Pesce plays everything from Gershwin to John Mayer. She’s performed with Jerry Lewis, Debbie Reynolds and Pat Boone, and performed special concerts for Shaquille O’Neal, Janet Napolitano and President George H. W. Bush.

location: 5040 W. Wild Horse Pass Blvd. Gila River Reservation, AZ, 85246
name: Dokken/Great White
description: Los Angeles hard rockers Dokken have sold more than 10 million albums worldwide, scoring hits with songs such as ""Alone Again," "Just Got Lucky" and "Dream Warriors." The group's latest album, "Lightning Strikes Again," debuted at No. 133 on the Billboard Top 200 chart. Dokken is joined by fellow Angelenos Great White, who scored hits throughout the 1980s with songs such as "Once Bitten, Twice Shy" and "Rock Me." The group released its latest record, "Rising," in 2009.

name: B/S - The Tribute to Bon Scott-era AC/DC
description: This Phoenix band pays tribute to the Bon Scott era of AC/DC, re-creating the look and sound of the Australian metal legends' 1979 live show. The band performs hits such as “High Voltage,” “Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap” and “It's a Long Way to the Top (If You Wanna Rock 'n' Roll).”

name: B/S - The Tribute to Bon Scott-era AC/DC
description: This Phoenix band pays tribute to the Bon Scott era of AC/DC, re-creating the look and sound of the Australian metal legends' 1979 live show. The band performs hits such as “High Voltage,” “Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap” and “It's a Long Way to the Top (If You Wanna Rock 'n' Roll).”

name: Black 'n Blue
description: This glam-rock band from Portland, Ore., was inducted into the Oregon Music Hall of Fame in 2010. The band recorded its last studio album,"In Heat," in 1988 and is set to release new album "Hell Yeah!" sometime in the next year. Metal bands 68 Guns and Hollow also perform at this 21-and-older show.

name: Pat Benatar and Neil Giraldo
description: Joined by her longtime guitarist and husband Neil Giraldo, rock legend Pat Benatar performs songs from throughout her career, including "Love Is A Battlefield" and "Hit Me With Your Best Shot." Benetar has earned two multi-platinum albums, five platinum albums and 19 Top 40 singles.

name: The Funeral Pyre
description: These black metal rockers out of California reunited with guitarist Justin Garcia for their latest album, 2010's "Vultures at Dawn." Metal bands the Secret and Music is the Enemy open this all-ages show.

location: 36460 N. Encanterra Drive San Tan Valley, AZ, 85140
name: The Good Life Festival
description: Encanterra hosts another edition of its Good Life Festival, this time bringing '70s hit makers Chicago to the Valley. Known for their horn-heavy brand of pop-rock, Chicago scored hits with songs such as "25 or 6 to 4," "Saturday in the Park." and "Hard Habit to Break." The group's career features 25 platinum albums, including five consecutive No.1 albums.

location: 5040 W. Wild Horse Pass Blvd. Gila River Reservation, AZ, 85246
name: Foreigner
description: These rock legends return to the Valley in support of their ninth album, 2009's "Can't Slow Down," the group's first since 1994 and the first to feature lead singer Kelly Hansen. Foreigner has sold more than 70 million albums worldwide, scoring a number of hits, including the No.1 single, "I Want to Know What Love Is."

name: "How Great Thou Art: The Gospel Music of Elvis Presley"
Amon Amarth
description: These Swedish death metal rockers perform the bruising tunes from their eighth album, this year's "Surtur Rising,"

name: Fear Factory
description: This Los Angeles heavy-metal band was a driving force in the genre during the mid-1990s, winning fans with its combination of thrash and groove metal. The band has performed at three Ozzfests and sold more than 1 million albums in the U.S. The band broke up in 2002 and reunited with a new lineup in 2009. The band released its most recent album, "Mechanize," in 2010.

name: The Moody Blues
description: Renowned for their poetic mixture of classical music and pop rock, this English band has sold more than 70 million albums worldwide, earning 14 platinum and gold albums. The band's sophomore album, 1967's "Days of Future Passed," formed the band's sound while scoring hits such as "Nights in White Satin" and "Tuesday Afternoon."

name: Rush
description: These Canadian prog-rock legends return to the Valley as part of their Time Machine Tour, this time performing their 1981 album "Moving Pictures" in its entity. The album is the group's biggest-selling to date, certified quadruple-platinum. The band has racked up 24 gold records and 14 platinum records over the course of its career. The group's set to release its 19th album, "Clockwork Angels," this year.

name: Musical Jam Session for Musicians with Memory Loss
description: The Banner Alzheimer’s Institute and the ASU Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts offers a free monthly “jam session” designed for musicians with memory loss issues. Participants and care partners are invited to bring their instruments to play or to sing along. Some instruments, including pianos, guitars and drums, are provided by ASU. Jams are held the first Friday of each month. Registration required.

name: Girl Talk
description: Pittsburgh DJ and producer Gregg Gillis, also known as Girl Talk, has become the unofficial "king of the mash-ups." Gillis has been winning over legions of fans with his high-energy dance tracks, which he creates by tightly weaving samples of popular hip-hop, rock and pop tracks into a single song. Girl Talk's 2008 album, "Feed the Animals," was named No. 4 on Time's "Top 10 Albums of 2008" list, and he released his fifth album, "All Day," in 2010. Electronic musicians Max Tundra and Junk Culture open this all-ages show.

name: Giant Wednesdays: Max Graham
description: This Canadian DJ and producer spins his brand of progressive house and trance techno, including his latest singles, 2010's "Nothing Else Matters" and "Dusky 2010 (Does She Know Yet)." A 21-and-older show.

name: Sticky Fingers
description: Friday nights, DJs William Reed, Prince $$, 2Tonedisco and Austin Head take over the rooftop bar at this downtown Phoenix spot, spinning a hip shaking mix of garage rock, classic rock and modern indie hits. Drink specials include $2 Pinnacle vodka drinks and $2 PBR.

name: Fuse Kick Off Party with Yolanda Be Cool
description: This Australian DJ duo hit the international scene with their 2010 single, "We No Speak Americano," which became a hit in a number of countries, ranking No. 29 on the US Billboard Hot 100. They are currently working on their first album. An 18-and-older show.

name: College DJ Competition
description: Saturday nights in March, aspiring college DJs are invited to hit the decks at this hot Scottsdale club for this weekly competition. DJs can spin hip-hop, electro or top 40. They are judged on their talent, ability and the crowd's reaction. DJs must have a current college ID. See website for details.

name: Wolfgang Gartner
description: This acclaimed electro house producer and DJ recently earned a Grammy nomination for best remixed recording for his remix of Andy Caldwell's "Funk Nasty." Gartner released a number of singles this year, including "Undertaker," "Conscindo" and "Animal Rights." A 16-and-older show.

name: Soundwave Music Festival
description: This electronic music festival features performances by headliners Diplo and Boys Noize, along with 20 other electronic artists. The park's waterslides are open during this 18-and-older event.

location: 2000 E. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Tequilazona!
description: Taste a variety of local and international tequilas, and sample appetizers paired with tequila at Market Place Plaza. Sonan Latin Jazz ensemble performs. A VIP area offers a rooftop party, premium margaritas, gourmet appetizers and a Tequilazona gift pack. Proceeds benefit Friends of Public Radio Arizona.

name: Club Rain
description: A Scottsdale address without the Scottsdale hype, Club Rain brings a fresh concept and Latino twist to the city. Check out traditional and Latin-influenced events, the red-roped VIP lounge and numerous plasma TVs. Hours and days open may vary.

name: Slick Rick
