description: This London-born rapper rose to prominence during the formative days of hip-hop music, scoring hits with song such as "La Di Da Di," "Mona Lisa" and "Children's Story." Known for his distinct British accent and his storytelling style, Slick Rick released his latest album, "The Art of Storytelling," in 1999 and has recently appeared on albums by Raekwon, Mos Def and Asher Roth. The concert features Rick performing his classic 1988 debut, "The Great Adventures of Slick Rick," in its entirety.

name: StrangeNoize Tour
description: This hip-hop tour features performances by headliners Krizz Kaliko and Johnny Richter of the Kottonmouth Kings. The tour also features performances by rappers Kutt Calhoun, Saigon, Potluck and Jhornay.

name: Murs
description: This Los Angeles alternative rapper arrives behind his latest album, 2008's "Murs for President," which debuted at No. 11 on the Billboard Rap chart and earned an 8/10 review from Spin. Murs also released a collaborative album with producer 9th Wonder, "Fornever," in 2010.

name: DJ Foundation
description: This Arizona hip-hop artist has worked with the Afro Classics, Drunken Immortals and the Insects, as well as underground hip-hop icon Murs.

name: Lil' Flip
description: Best know for the songs "Sunshine" and "Game Over (Flip)," this Houston rapper has scored two platinum albums and has appeared on albums by Three 6 Mafia, Young Money and Chamillionaire. He released his most recent album, "Ahead of My Time," in 2010.

name: Talib Kweli
description: This celebrated New York hip-hop artist first rose to fame with his group Black Star, a collaboration with Mos Def. Know for his interesting samples and literate lyrics, Kweli has collaborated with Kayne West, Common and Questlove. Kweli arrives in support of his fourth album, 2010's "Gutter Rainbows."

name: Soulja Boy
description: This Chicago rapper scored a huge hit with his 2007 single, "Crank That (Soulja Boy)," which hit No. 1 on the Billboard 100, inspired a dance craze and earned a Grammy nomination for Best Rap Song. He arrives in support of his third album, 2010's "The DeAndre Way."

name: Lil Wayne
description: This Grammy Award-winning rapper returns to the Valley behind his eighth album, 2010's "I Am Not a Human Being," which debuted at No. 2 on the US Billboard 200 chart. The tour is Lil Wayne's first major tour since serving an eight-month prison sentence in New York, and "I Am Not a Human Being" is his hip-hop follow-up to his multi-platinum 2008 breakthrough, "Tha Carter III." Lil Wayne recently released his new single, "6 Foot 7 Foot," the first song off his heavily anticipated "The Carter IV" album, slated to be released this year. Rappers Nicki Minaj, Rick Ross and Travis Barker and Mixmaster also perform at this all-ages show.

name: Mad Rad
description: These Seattle-based dance-rappers have been hipster blog favorites since the release of their debut record, 2008's "White Gold." The band arrives behind its sophomore release, 2010's "The Youth Die Young." Rock band the Premiere opens this show.

location: 5040 W. Wild Horse Pass Blvd. Gila River Reservation, AZ, 85246
name: Diddy-Dirty Money Tour featuring Sean “Diddy” Combs
description: Rap mogul Sean "Diddy" Combs performs with his latest project, Diddy-Dirty Money, featuring singers Dawn Richards and Kalenna Harper, playing songs from the group's debut album, 2010's "Last Train to Paris." The head of Bad Boy Records, Combs helped launch the careers of the Notorious B.I.G. and a number of other big rappers, while scoring his own hits starting with his 1997 Grammy Award-winning debut "No Way Out." In addition, Combs also heads the clothing line Sean John, a movie production company and two restaurants. He's also appeared in several movies and is the producer of MTV's "Making the Band."

name: Tech N9ne
description: This Kansas City, Mo., rapper arrives in support of his latest record, this year's "All 6’s And 7’s," which features collaborations with T-Pain, Lil Wayne, and Yelawolf. The album is the followup to Tech N9ne's 2010 release, "The Gates Mixed Plate."

name: Obscura
description: Resident DJs Roya and Funkfinger entertain by spinning Britpop, indie, '80s new wave and mod tunes. The dance party highlights upcoming CD releases. Drink specials include $3 well drinks and $2 house pints. Age 21 and older.

name: Tranzylvania
description: Arizona's largest goth/industrial club. DJs spin EBM, gothic, industrial and synthpop music. For ages 21 and older from 10 p.m.-2 a.m. For ages 18 and older from 2-3:30 a.m.

name: The Kickback
description: Sunday afternoons on the patio of Padre's offers patrons drink specials, live music and a chance to socialize. Enjoy $4 sangrias, $3 domestics, $2 domestic drafts and a $5 food menu. Resident DJs spin a variety of tunes.

name: Salsa Night
description: Salsa classes and dancing, with a DJ and live entertainment. For ages 21 and older.

name: Chasers Bar and Nightclub
description: Back in the day, this club earned a reputation for being a regular meeting ground for the gothy dance crowd. Chasers is known for evenings filled with loud rock and metal acts as well as special events. Monday nights, the mike is open to anyone wanting to take their chance belting it out in this giant room, solo or with a band. You can even pause the head banging for a game of shuffleboard, pool, foosball or something in the video game realm.

name: Spring Fling
description: Bell Mar Plaza thanks customers with six weeks of events. Activities include live music, an art show, food, wine and beer tastings, balloons for kids, a fashion show, a car show and etching classes. Saturday event times vary. A detailed event schedule is available online.

location: 12351 W. Indian School Road Avondale, AZ, 85392
name: Soulful Showcase Sundays
description: On second and forth Sundays of the month, this Avondale bar plays host to up-and-coming comedians, musicians, singers and poets. Admission includes a chicken and waffle dinner.

name: Adult Skate Night
description: Skaters 16 and older can roll around the rink to R&B and rock and roll music. Skate rental is additional or bring your own. An arcade features pinball and video games and snacks are available from the cafe.

name: Jazz Thursdays
description: Every Thursday night for the past 10 years, musicians from across the Valley have performed at this Chandler eatery, playing a mix of jazz, rock, blues and pop music.

location: The Buttes 2000 Westcourt Way Tempe, AZ, 85282
name: Chuck E. Baby and the All Stars
description: This local band rocks this resort bar every Saturday night, performing a range of classic rock tunes, blues tracks and original songs. Songs off the group's first album, "Never in a Million Years," were picked up by MTV and used in several episodes of the series "The Real World."

location: 10455 E. Pinnacle Peak Parkway Scottsdale, AZ, 85255
name: Renee Patrick
description: This Phoenix based pop/gospel/jazz artist comes from a musical family. Her father was a member of the doo-wop group the Ink Spots, and her mother recorded duets with Terry Johnson of the Flamingos. Patrick performs pop and jazz tunes with emotion and energy.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Miniature Tigers
description: These indie-poppers might live in Brooklyn now, but they cut their teeth playing shows around the Valley. Led by Phoenix native Charlie Brand, the Miniature Tigers specialize in catchy, sunny indie rock songs, and were named "one of the 25 best bands on Myspace" by Rolling Stone in 2006. The band released its sophomore effort, "Fortress," in 2010. Indie rockers Pepper Rabbit open this all-ages show.

name: Dashboard Confessional
description: Celebrating the 10th anniversary of his debut album, 2000's "The Swiss Army Romance," Florida singer-songwriter Chris Carrabba, the man behind Dashboard Confessional, performs a solo acoustic show. Carrabba's emotional songwriting has landed him hits such as "Screaming Infidelities," "Hands Down" and "Vindicated," and he's earned three gold records. His latest album, 2009's "Alter the Ending," debuted at No. 19 on the Billboard 200 chart.

location: 3 S. Second St., Suite 117 Phoenix, AZ, 85004
name: Kinch
description: These Phoenix indie-rockers have been making big waves across the country with their brand of stomping indie-pop, drawing comparisons to everyone from Ben Folds and the Arcade Fire to 1960s British invasion groups. A long time favorite on the local scene, Kinch's debut album, "Advances," was named "Best Arizona Album of 2008" by the Phoenix New Times.

name: Toad the Wet Sprocket
description: These California alt-rockers scored a number of hits in the '90s with songs such as "Walk on the Ocean," "Something's Always Wrong" and "Fall Down." The group recently announced its official reunion and is currently writing songs for a new studio album, its first since 1997's "Coil."

name: Boneyard
description: Led by Phoenix guitarist Carole Pellatt, this Valley four-piece performs jazzy evenings of experimental grooves and instrumental jam sessions.

name: The Baseball Project
description: This indie-rock supergroup features Peter Buck of R.E.M., Scott McCaughey of the Young Fresh Fellows and the Minus 5 and Steve Wynn of Dream Syndicate. True to its name, the band's first album, 2008's "Volume 1: Frozen Ropes and Dying Quails," and 2009 EP, "Homerun," both pay power-pop homage to the game of baseball.

location: 3 S. Second St., Suite 117 Phoenix, AZ, 85004
name: Lady Gaga After Party with Super Stereo
description: After the Lady Gaga concert at US Airways Center, head across the street to the Hard Rock Cafe and check out Tempe's Super Stereo. Combining pulsing electro indie-pop with wistful vocals and plenty of hooks, the group performs the danceable songs from its debut album, 2010's “This is Electropop.” A 21-and-older show.

name: Lords of Acid
description: Known for their outrageously sexual lyrics and their pounding electronic music, these Belgian post-industrial rockers hit the rave scene with their controversial 1988 single "I Sit on Acid." The group has sold more than 1.5 million albums worldwide and is set to release a new album this year, its first in more than 10 years. Electronic bands Angel Spit, Radical G and Chant also perform at this 18-and-older show.

name: Katastro
description: Combining elements of hip-hop, blues, rock and funk, these Tempe rockers have toured with groups such as the Dirty Heads, Method Man, Redman and Ghostface Killah. The group released its latest EP, "Poking Holes in a Pattern," in 2009, and recently hit the road with Tomorrow's Bad Seeds and Passafire. Local bands Seedless and the Veragroove also perform at this all-ages show.

location: 1423 S. Country Club Drive Mesa, AZ, 85210
name: The Persuaders
description: The Persuaders are a new local band, making their debut at this Goat Head Saloon show. The band features members of the Pistoleros, Dead Hot Workshop and the Gin Blossoms. Local rock bands Franko Ditty Danko, Michael Treatch, A Few Random Drunks and Creepy Jack also perform at this 21-and-older show.

name: Free Outdoor Concert: Otis & The Beat

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: B-Side Players
description: This large San Diego band plays a high-energy blend of Cuban, Jamaican and Mexican music, blending the traditional sounds with elements of funk, rock, jazz and hip-hop. The B-Side Players have performed with bands such as the Wailers, Ben Harper and Ozomatli, and released their latest album, "Radio Afro Mexica," in 2009. A 21-and-older show.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Men
description: Featuring JD Samson of indie-electronic band Le Tigre, this Brooklyn-based art and music collective focuses on wild live performances, as well as hyperactive dance tunes. The band is set to released its debut album this year.

name: Rebelution
description: The debut album by this Santa Barbara, Calif., reggae band, 2007's "Courage to Grow," reached No. 4 on the Billboard Reggae Album chart. The band released its follow-up, "Bright Side of Life," in 2009.

location: 5040 W. Wild Horse Pass Blvd. Gila River Reservation, AZ, 85246
name: Blues Traveler
description: Led by harmonica virtuoso John Popper, these New Jersey alt-rockers hit it big with their Grammy Award-winning 1994 single "Run Around," which hit No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart. Known for jammy live shows, the group arrives behind its ninth album, 2008's "North Hollywood Shootout."

name: The Author
description: These Mesa hardcore rockers celebrate the release of their new EP, "Your Young." Rock bands the Fair and Debonair, Run With the Hunted, Red Son, Georgianna Hawkins and Before You Fled also perform at this all-ages show.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Brendan James and Matt White
description: New York singer-songwriter Brendan James preforms the songs from his self-titled sophomore album, which debuted at No. 93 on the Billboard 200 chart. He's joined by fellow New Yorker Matt White, playing songs from his latest record, 2010's "It's the Good Crazy." Singer-songwriter Laura Pritchard also performs at this 21-and-older show.

name: War of Ages
description: These Christian metalcore rockers from Erie, Penn., perform the hardcore songs from their fourth album, 2010's "Eternal, which hit No. 179 on the Billboard 200 chart. Rock bands Onward to Olympus, Your Memorial, As Hell Retreats and Gideon also perform at this all-ages show.

name: Four Year Strong
description: These punk rockers from Worcester, Mass., have earned a huge following with their blend of hardcore and pop punk. The group's third album, 2010's "Enemy of the World," debuted at No. 40 on the Billboard 200 charts. Punk band Go Great Guns opens this all-ages show.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Papercuts
description: Centered around San Francisco singer-songwriter Jason Robert Quever, these California indie-rockers perform the lo-fi dream pop from their fourth album, 2011's "Fading Parade." London indie-rockers Banjo or Freakout also perform at this all-ages show.

name: A Day to Remember
description: These Florida rockers have found a winning combination with their blend of metalcore and pop punk, with their most recent album, 2010's "What Separates Me from You," reaching No. 11 on the Billboard 200 chart. Metalcore bands Bring Me the Horizon, Pierce the Veil and We Came as Romans also perform at this all-ages show.

name: British Sea Power
description: Known for their dynamic live shows, these English rockers have been indie-pop favorites since the release of their sophomore album, 2005's "Open Season." The group arrives behind its latest album, 2010's "Valhalla Dancehall." Indie rockers A Classic Education opens this all-ages show.

name: All Time Low
description: This Baltimore pop punk band was named Alternative Press magazine's "Band of the Year" in 2008, and its 2009 album, "Nothing Personal," hit No. 1 on the U.S. Alternative Albums charts. The band arrives behind its latest, 2011's "Dirty Work." Punk bands Yellowcard, Hey Monday and the Summer Set open this all-ages show.

name: Voxhaul Broadcast
description: These Los Angeles indie-rockers blend their Beatles-esque tunes with elements of R&B and soul. The group has been stars in the United Kingdom and has appeared at the Noisepop Pop Fest in San Francisco. The group arrives behind its latest album, 2011's "Timing is Everything." A 21-and-older show.

name: The Plurals
description: This power-punk trio from Lansing, Mich., arrives in support of its latest record, 2011's "The Plurals Today, The Plurals Tomorrow: A Futurospective."

name: The Dangerous Summer
description: The debut album by these Maryland indie-punks, 2009's "Reach for the Sun," hit No. 42 on the Billboard Top Heatseekers charts. The group is working on a followup. Rock bands Sparks the Rescue, the Graduate and the Scenic open this all-ages show.

name: Protest the Hero
description: After stints on the Warped Tour and tours with bands such as Killswitch Engage, Alexisonfire and Bullet For My Valentine, the latest album by this Canadian metal group find them moving in a more progressive, experimental direction. Rock bands Maylene and the Sons of Disaster and Tesseract also perform at this all-ages show.

name: Arcade Fire
description: Fresh off their win for "Album of the Year" at this year's Grammy Awards, these celebrated Canadian indie-rockers arrive in the Valley in support of their third album, 2010's "The Suburbs." Known for their cinematic blend of driving indie-folk rock and lead singer Win Butler's intense vocals, the group has been critically celebrated since its 2004 debut "Funeral." Upon its release, "The Suburbs" hit No. 1 on the U.S. Billboard 200 charts and appeared on the best of 2010 lists from Spin, Pitchfork, NPR, Rolling Stone and many more. Los Angeles indie-rockers Local Natives open this all-ages show.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Fervor Records Artist Showcase
description: The indie record label shows off some of its top artists at this showcase, featuring performances by Super Stereo and Tarik NuClothes. President Gator offers a DJ set. A 21-and-older show.

name: The Black Keys
description: Playing their hard-driving brand of blues-influences garage rock, these Akron, Ohio, rockers have been critical favorites and underground heroes for nearly a decade. Known for its exhaustive touring schedule, the band scored a big breakthrough with its sixth album, 2010's "Brothers," which hit No. 3 on the Billboard 200 and was ranked No. 2 on Rolling Stone magazine's "Best Albums of 2010" list. The Black Keys were also named "Artist of the Year" by Spin magazine. Indie-rock bands Cage the Elephant and the Stone Foxes also perform at this all-ages show.

name: The New Pornographers
description: These celebrated Canadian indie-rockers have been critical darlings and indie-rock favorites since the release of their debut album, 2000's "Mass Romantic." The band's fifth album, 2010's "Together," debuted at No. 18 on the Billboard 200 chart and earned a 9/10 review from PopMatters magazine. Indie-rockers Menomena open this all-ages show.

location: 7025 E. Via Soleri Drive Scottsdale, AZ, 85251
name: GreenStock Concerts: Candlebox
description: Performing as part of the GreenStock Expo, these Seattle alternative rockers perform songs from their latest album, 2008's "Into the Sun." Candlebox's 1993 self-titled debut featured the hit "Far Behind" and was certified quadruple platinum. The group scored other radio hits and performed as part of Woodstock '94.

name: Biffy Clyro
description: These Scottish indie-rockers arrive behind their fourth album, 2009's "Only Revolutions." The record has been certified platinum in the UK and was nominated for the 2010 Mercury Prize, which is awarded annually for the best album in the United Kingdom or Ireland.

name: Jeff Dahl
description: This punk rock singer-songwriter from Hawaii has served time in punk bands such as Vox Pop, Powertrip and the Angry Samoans. Dahl has released more than 26 albums since his debut single, 1977's "Rock N Roll Critic."

name: Super Happy Funtime Burlesque
description: This sexy musical comedy theater troupe from Grand Rapids, Mich., presents an evening full of laughs, sideshow tricks, magic acts and sexy striptease shows. The End of Times Orchestra adds in a mix of jazz, Zydeco and polka music. Local burlesque troupe Provocatease also performs at this 21-and-older show.

name: (Sic)monic
description: Creating a heavy mixture of jazz fusion, prog-rock and heavy metal, this Phoenix band released its sophomore album, “Somnambulist,” in 2010.

name: Race You There EP Release Show
description: These Tucson indie-rockers celebrate the release of their new EP, "Catalyst." Local rockers What Laura Says, Milo the Mayor and Madera Strand also perform at this 21-and-older show.

location: 7025 E. Via Soleri Drive Scottsdale, AZ, 85251
name: GreenStock Concerts: Carolina Liar
description: These Los Angeles alt-rockers perform songs from their 2008 debut album, "Coming to Terms," which hit No. 3 on the Billboard Heatseekers chart and featured the hit single, "Show Me What I'm Looking For."

name: Lake
description: These Olympia, Wash., indie-rockers perform the sunny indie-pop off their latest record, 2010's "Let's Build A Roof." Indie-rockers Ages and Ages and French Quarter also perform at this all-ages show.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Titus Andronicus
description: The New Jersey indie-punks were named one of the best new bands of 2010 by Rolling Stone. The group's most recent album, 2010's "The Monitor," is a loose concept album about the Civil War and was ranked No. 10 on Pitchfork's "Best of 2010" list.

name: Subhumans
description: These influential English hardcore punks formed in 1980, and have split up a couple of times since. The group released its latest album, "Internal Riot," in 2007. Punk bands MDC and the Grim open this all-ages show.

name: CSS
description: These Brazilian New Rave rockers perform their danceable mix of indie-rock and electronica. Singing in both English and Portuguese, the group performs songs from its latest release, 2008's "Donkey."

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: The Joy Formidable
description: Led by the frantic vocals of lead singer Ritzy Bryan, these Welsh indie-rockers have toured with bands such as the Temper Trap, the Editors and Passion Pit. The group released its debut EP, "A Balloon Called Moaning," in 2010, and is set to release its debut album, "The Big Roar," this year.

name: Pinback
description: The latest album by these San Diego indie-rockers, 2007's "Autumn of the Seraphs," earned a 7.8/10 review from Pitchfork, and debuted at No. 3 on the Billboard Independence Album Charts. The group recently made a guest appearance on the TV show "Yo Gabba Gabba!," and is currently working a new album.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Joe Purdy
description: This Arkansas singer-songwriter adds his soulful voice to the delicate folk songs from his latest album, "This American."

name: The Green
description: Hailing from Oahu, Hawaii, these reggae rockers incorporate elements of their Hawaiian music into their root-reggae sound. The group's 2010 self-titled debut album was named iTunes' "Best Reggae Album of 2010." Reggae band Fortunate Youth open this 21-and-older show.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: The Growlers
description: These Los Angeles indie-rockers play a boozy blend of surf rock and garage rock. Known for their wild live shows, the group arrives behind its latest album, 2010's "Hot Tropics." California indie-rockers Allah-Las also perform at this 21-and-older show.

name: Parallels
description: Featuring ex-Crystal Castles drummer and composer Cameron Findlay, this Canadian synth-pop duo performs songs from its debut album, 2010's "Visionaries." A 21-and-older show.

name: Music in the Garden: Dry River Yacht Club
description: Tempe's Dry River Yacht Club features French horns, bassoons and accordions. The group plays a high-energy brand of Gypsy-folk. The band released its latest album, "The Ugliest Princess," in 2010. This popular event also features a chef-attended food station featuring weekly specials for an additional charge and a cash bar. A 21-and-older event.

location: 3 S. Second St., Suite 117 Phoenix, AZ, 85004
name: Ron Pope
description: Marked by his soulful voice and introspective lyrics, this New York City singer-songwriter performs songs from his new album, this year's "Whatever It Takes." Singer-songwriters Ari Herstand and Zach Berkman open this all-ages show.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Royal Bangs
description: These Knoxville indie-rockers were discovered on MySpace by Black Keys drummer Patrick Carney and quickly signed to his Audio Eagle Records label. With a sound that combines garage rock and modern indie rock, the group arrives in support of its second album, 2009's "Let It Beep." Indie-rockers Superhumanoids open this all-ages show.

name: The Dirty Heads
description: Playing the laid-back blend of reggae and ska pioneered by bands like Sublime, these mellow Southern California rockers have toured with O.A.R., 311, Pepper and the Kottonmouth Kings. The group released its debut album, "Any Port in a Storm," in 2008.

name: Jethro Tull
description: Celebrating the 40th anniversary of their celebrated 1971 release, "Aqualung," these English rockers perform the album in its entirety, along with a number of other favorites.

name: Chicks with Picks
description: Founded by Valley musicians Pandy Raye and Rhonda Hitchcock, Chicks with Picks is made up of more than 75 female singer-songwriters and musicians from across the Valley. The group’s performances are often folky, acoustic affairs and feature a rotating list of performers. Performing on the District Stage.

location: 16844 N. Arrowhead Fountains Center Drive Peoria, AZ, 85382
name: The Jimmy Buffett Tribute Party
description: Local band the Stinson Brotherz invite visitors to Margaritaville with their Jimmy Buffett tribute show, donning Hawaiian shirts and straw hats for hits like "Cheeseburger in Paradise," "Volcano" and "Fins." Show times at 4 and 6:30 p.m.

name: Mary Hoffman
description: This Phoenix country signer has opened for Kenny Chesney, Keith Urban, Sammy Hagar and Michelle Branch, and made it into the top 10 in the Arizona Idol competition. With funky guitar playing and a powerful voice, Hoffman performs songs from her latest album, "Somebody Else."

location: 6033 E. Cave Creek Road Cave Creek, AZ, 85331
name: Jeordie
venue: Cave Creek Coffee Co. and Wine Purveyors
description: Blending modern pop tunes with folk guitar, this Phoenix singer-songwriter has performed as a supporting act for Dido, Jewel, Indigo Girls, Sade and Brooks & Dunn. She also recently releases a 23-track live album called "Bootleg."

location: 102 N. Old Litchfield Road Litchfield Park, AZ, 85340
name: Mary Hoffman
description: This Phoenix country signer has opened for Kenny Chesney, Keith Urban, Sammy Hagar and Michelle Branch and made it into the top 10 in the Arizona Idol competition. With funky guitar playing and a powerful voice, Hoffman performs songs from her latest album, "Somebody Else." Performing every Thursday night.

name: Balinese Gamelan Workshop
description: Curatorial assistant Colin Pearson leads this workshop to introduce students to Balinese music and culture. Guests 12 and older can play the Balinese instruments. No musical experience necessary. Workshops held the first and third Thursdays of the month through May. Group discounts available. See website for details.

location: 700 W. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: "Walk-in Wednesdays"
description: Tempe singer-songwriter Walt Richardson hosts this popular open mike series, which invites musicians of all genres to perform. A youth segment for players high school age and younger is held from 5 to 6 p.m. The audience can enjoy food and beverage specials from Santa Barbara Catering.

name: Live Acoustic Music
description: Live music and entertainment is offered on Friday nights. The coffee house is open on the campus of First Baptist Church of Scottsdale with Nancy Gee performing live jazz June 19, and Rod DiGiovanni playing acoustic folk/country on June 26.

location: 7500 E. Doubletree Ranch Road Scottsdale, AZ, 85258
name: Mosaico
venue: Hyatt Regency Scottsdale Resort and Spa at Gainey Ranch
description: This Arizona flamenco group performs original music inspired by the sounds of Spain, Latin America and the Caribbean. Incorporating guitar, bass, flute, violin, piano and percussion, the group adds a taste of the Southwest to their performance. Performing in the hotel's lobby bar.

name: Hot Buttered Rum
description: This San Fransisco progressive bluegrass group performs its jammy blend of folk, rock and reggae. The band has performed at the Telluride Bluegrass Festival, the Newport Folk Festival, South by Southwest and the Bonnaroo Music Festival and released its latest album, "Limbs Akimbo," in 2009. A 21-and-older show.

name: American Songbook With Philip Brunelle and Friends
price: $15, $13 for age 64 and older, $10 for ages 6-17, free for age 5 and younger
description: Join VocalEssence artistic director Philip Brunelle as emcee and pianist for an evening of cabaret with soprano Maria Jette and baritone Bradley Greenwald. The trio celebrates the American Songbook in a private reception. Seating is on a first-come, first-seated basis. Call or see website to purchase tickets.

name: Hi-Country Bluegrass Festival
description: This musical festival features performances by bluegrass bands the Hey Boyz, Copper River Band, Igor's Jazz Cowboys, Shuler Family Band, Tangled Strings and the Trusting Heart Band.

location: 5700 W. North Loop Road Gila River Reservation, AZ, 85226
name: Steve Barker Band
description: Led by singer Steve Barker, this Phoenix band performs traditional country tunes and classic Western songs. The group has released two albums, "20 Classic Songs" and "The Last Cowboy Song," and performs at Rawhide every week.

name: Obscura
description: Resident DJs Roya and Funkfinger entertain by spinning Britpop, indie, '80s new wave and mod tunes. The dance party highlights upcoming CD releases. Drink specials include $3 well drinks and $2 house pints. Age 21 and older.

name: Local DJ Night
description: Grooves and tunes are spun twice a week. Grab your drink and shake what you got along to the beats created by local DJs.

name: Daedelus with Tokimonsta
description: Los Angeles DJ and producer Daedelus creates experimental soundscapes, using real instruments alongside electronic elements. He released his latest album, "Bespoke," in 2011. Fellow Los Angeles producer Tokimonsta also performs. Both DJs are scheduled to play at this year's Coachella Music and Art Festival.

name: Music in Motion
price: $15, $13 for age 65 and older, $10 for ages 6-17, free for age 5 and younger
description: Enjoy an evening of cocktails and blues. Groove to the sounds of Big Daddy D and the Dynamites, who perform in the courtyard. Free with museum admission. At 9 p.m., head to the Compound Grill for Americana music by the Band of Heathens. Show your museum receipt to get in for $5. Cash only for a no-host bar.

location: 2155 E. University Drive, Suite 116 Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Shake That Azz 2
description: This electronic music event features West Coast future bass, glitch hop and electro courtesy of DJs Lando Kal of Lazer Sword and Comma, along with psychedelic artworks by Erika Jaynes. A 21-and-older show.

name: Giant Wednesdays: Laidback Luke
description: This Dutch house DJ and producer has worked with such artists as David Guetta, Axwell, Junior Sanchez and Steve Angello, and was ranked No. 17 on DJ Mag's Top 100 DJ list in 2010. Laidback Luke recently collaborated with Steve Aoki and Lil Jon for his latest single, 2011's "Turbulence." DJ Tranzit also performs at this 21-and-older show.

name: The Colossal Event
description: This two-day music festival features DJs and electronic musicians from around the country on two stages. Day 1 features performances by Chase & Status Jakes, TV Rock, HavocNdeeD, Radar, Louder, Mike Saga, Aly & Fila, Graham, Space Rockerz, Jordan Stevens, Sean Essex and DJ Lujan. The line-up for Day 2 features Steve Aoki, Felguk, Felix Cartal, Turner & Heit, Michael James, Jack Beats, Nero, Liquid Stranger, Style of Eye, Tranzit and Jared Alan.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Dirty Vegas
description: This British house music trio hit it big with its 2001 single "Days Go By," which first hit the mainstream after being featured in a commercial for the 2003 Mitsubishi Eclipse. The song hit No. 14 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 chart and earned the group a Grammy for Best Dance Recording. The group was on hiatus for many years, but released its first album in seven years, "Electric Love," this year. A 21-and-older show.

name: Giant Wednesdays: Gareth Emery
description: This celebrated English trance producer and DJ was ranked No. 7 in DJ Mag's 2010 Top 100 DJs Poll. Emery arrives in support of his latest release, 2011's "Northern Lights Re-Lit." A 21-and-older show.

name: Giant Wednesdays: Danny Howells
description: This English DJ spins his mix of progressive, tribal and tech house tunes, including tracks from his latest release, 2009's "Dig Deeper: The New Label." A 21-and-older show.

name: Giant Wednesdays: Nick Warren
description: This English house DJ and producer released eight albums as part of the acclaimed Global Underground series. He and DJ Jody Wisternoff form the electronic duo Way Out West. Warren released his latest album, "In Search of Silver, " this year. DJs Turner & Heit and Christian James also perform at this 21-and-older show.

name: Cut Copy
description: Drawling heavily from 1980s New Wave, these Australian electropoppers arrive in support of their third album, 2011's "Zonoscope," which hit No. 46 on the US Billboard 200 chart.

name: FUSE Fridays
description: Every Friday night, this Sc hotspot features a host of local and national DJs spinning some of the hottest dance and electronic beats. The party is offered on two floors, with the rooftop dominated by heavy electro tracks and the downstairs pounding out progressive/tech grooves.

location: 4050 E. Chandler Heights Road Chandler, AZ, 85249
name: Sonoran Sunset Concert Series: Step’s Junk Funk
description: This Tempe musical group merges percussion with movement arts, creating music out of items found in the garbage. They also perform coordinated dance numbers.

name: "The Art of War"
description: The ASU Sinfonietta provides an evening of music with such well-known works as “Ride of the Valkyries” with a joint exhibition featuring new work inspired by the music of the concert and a martial arts demonstration. Viewing hours begin at 6:30 p.m. with the concert starting at 7:30.

location: 2000 E. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Pete Pancrazi
description: This jazz guitarist has been playing in the Valley since the early 1990s, and has been named jazz guitar player of the year by the AzJazz Magazine Readers' Poll. He'll perform songs from his four albums, including "Trio Songbook" and "Stand Alone."

name: AZ Diamond
description: Sing along with all your favorite Neil Diamond hits as this Phoenix tribute band delivers a high-energy, showstopping performance. Featuring Diamond lookalike Eddie Kij on vocals, the group performs songs such as "Cherry Cherry," "Sweet Caroline," "I'm a Believer," "America," "Kentucky Woman" and "Cracklin' Rosie."

name: Ameri"CAN" Craft Beer Festival
description: More than 40 local and national breweries attend this festival and expo, which features canned craft beer judging, tasting and educational seminars. There is also a beer science garden, live music and food. The crowd picks a People's Choice award. Admission includes a collectible, 4-ounce sample can. VIP access includes a VIP beer garden; a free copy of “The Beer Can” signed by its author, Richard Susa; a brewer meet-and-greet; unlimited food and treats; and special seating at the awards ceremony. Presented by Whole Foods Market and Draft Magazine. Must be 21 or older with ID. A portion of proceeds benefits Ear Candy, a charity that provides young people with access to music education.

location: 6640 S. Kings Ranch Road Gold Canyon, AZ, 85218
name: JJ Heller
description: This contemporary Christian music singer-songwriter has scored hits with songs such as "Your Hands" and "What Love Really Means." Her YouTube videos have become a sensation. Heller, who is based in Phoenix, released her latest album, "When I'm With You," in 2010.

name: The Daylights
description: These Los Angeles pop rockers toured with Katy Perry in 2009, and have hit the road alongside OneRepublic and Civil Twilight since then. The trio arrives behind their self-titled 2010 album.

name: Jordin Sparks and Friends
description: This special benefit concert kicks off the museum's first anniversary celebration featuring performances by Grammy-nominated artist Jordin Sparks, songwriter Marshall “Soulful” Jones and RFI Discoveries Music Award winner Maurice Kirya. Cocktails, hors d’oeuvres and museum admission on April 30 or May 1 are included.

name: Guy Pennacchio
description: This stylish singer pays tribute to the music of Frank Sinatra, singing songs such as "Fly Me To the Moon," "My Way" and "Witchcraft."

name: Herb Alpert and Lani Hall
description: Grammy Award winner Herb Alper of Herb Alpert & the Tijuana Brass and A&M Records fame performs with his wife, singer Lani Hall. The duo perform songs from their latest collaboration, 2011's "I Feel You." The concert features songs such as Van Morrison's "Moondance" and "Here Comes The Sun," and the Beatles' "Blackbird."

name: Wormrot
description: These grindcore rockers from Singapore arrive behind their heavy sophomore album, this year's "Dirge." Metal bands Landmine Marathon and Cagematch also perform at this all-ages show.

name: Melanie and Van
description: This acoustic duo performs a wide range of songs, including music by Elvis Presley, the Eagles, Patsy Cline, Johnny Cash, Shania Twain, Ray Charles and Aretha Franklin.

name: Kongos
description: This Phoenix indie-rock group is a band of brothers - Johnny, Jesse, Dylan and Daniel Kongos, sons of British singer-songwriter John Kongos. The group's sparkling, Beatles-inspired indie-rock landed it the award for best rock band of Phoenix in 2007 from the Phoenix New Times; Kongos recently released a new EP, “Aficanized Killer Beats.”

location: 7025 E. Via Soleri Drive Scottsdale, AZ, 85251
name: GreenStock Concerts: Fireflight
description: Performing as part of the GreenStock Expo, these Christian rockers from Florida perform songs from their Grammy-nominated fourth album, 2010's "For Those Who Wait."

name: My Genuine Find
description: This pop rock group is the brainchild of New Mexico singer-songwriter Bobby Mares. My Genuine Find arrive in support of their debut EP, "Love Enough." Rock bands New Age Cinema and Consider Me Dead open this all-ages show.

name: Zechs Marquise
description: These El Paso, Texas, rockers combine elements of progressive rock and punk, playing songs from their 2009 debut album, "Our Delicate Stranded Nightmare."

location: 3 S. Second St., Suite 117 Phoenix, AZ, 85004
name: Fake Problems
description: These Florida indie-rockers play a vintage rock and roll-inspired blend of punk-rock, landing them tours with Against Me! and the Gaslight Anthem. The group arrives in support of its latest album, 2010's "Real Ghosts Caught on Tape." Rock bands Pomegranates, Laura Stevenson and the Cans and Now, Now Every Children also perform at this all-ages show.

name: Arizona Homegrown
description: This show features Arizona musicians Quick Henry, Mojo Farmer, Walt Richardson, Angelique White and the Paper Showmen.

name: Roger Clyne and the Peacemakers
description: These Arizona musical staples perform songs from their latest album, 2011’s "Unida Cantina." Clyne first grabbed national attention while in the Tempe-based rock band the Refreshments, who scored a hit in 1996 with "Banditos." Since then, Clyne and his band of Southwestern troubadours have remained an Arizona favorite, winning over fans with their signature brand of party rock.

name: Civet
description: Self-described as a "femme fatale punk rock" band, these Long Beach, Calif., punks have toured alongside the Mighty Mighty Bosstones, the Dropkick Murphys and Social Distortion. The group released its latest album, "Love & War," earlier this year. Punk band Continental opens this all-ages show.

name: Concerts in the Park Series: PWK
description: This band of Gilbert teenagers, whose name stands for “People Worth Knowing,” perform their brand of sunny, pop rock. The band’s first singles, “All I Wanna Do” and “Gonna Be Me,” are up on iTunes, and the band is preparing its first album.

name: Shopping Kart Tragedies
description: These Gilbert indie-rockers perform their pop-punk tunes, joined by local rockers the Crush and Beauxmont.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Radar Bros.
description: These long-running Los Angeles indie-rockers recently toured with Modest Mouse and Teenage Fanclub and released their latest album, "The Illustrated Garden," in 2010.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: No Joy
description: Taking cues from the distortion-heavy sound of bands such as Sonic Youth and My Bloody Valentine, these Montreal noise rockers recently toured with Surfer Blood and Young Prisms. The group released its debut album, "Ghost Blonde," last year. Indie-rockers Weird Ladies open this all-ages show.

name: Dirty Beaches
description: Known for his rich baritone, dark, vintage rock style and pompadour hairstyle, Canadian singer-songwriter Alex Zhang Hungtai brings his musical project Dirty Beaches to the Valley. The group released its latest album, "Badlands," this year.

name: Xtra Ticket
description: Take a trip back in time and jam out to the songs of the Grateful Dead with this Tempe tribute band. The group's been together since 1994, and each member takes on a character from the Grateful Dead, creating faithful re-creations of some of the band's most iconic songs. A 21-and-older show.

location: 2000 E. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Hello Swindon
description: These Tempe rockers performs their eclectic blend of rock, R&B, funk and jazz, complete with saxophone riffs and groovy jams, drawing comparisons to groups like the Dave Matthews Band. The group performs music from its 2010 album “Alfalfa Centauri.”

name: Stephen Marley
description: The son of reggae legends Bob and Rita Marley, this Jamaican reggae artist has performed as a solo artists and as a member of Ziggy Marley and the Melody Makers. Stephen Marley produced his brother Damian Marley's Grammy award winning 2005 record "Welcome to Jamrock," and he released his latest solo album,"Revelation Part 1: Root of Life," this year.

location: 2000 E. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Casey Lee Smith
description: This 18-year-old country singer-songwriter from Glendale was the winner of the "Gospel/Inspiration" category in the 2009 John Lennon Songwriting Contest for his tune "Never Stood Taller." Smith's new album, "Chasin' Tin Cans," is due out this year.

location: 3 S. Second St., Suite 117 Phoenix, AZ, 85004
name: Rock to Cure
description: Rock out to a line-up of local musicians including Dust Jacket, Snail Quail and Hunger Artists. Proceeds from ticket sales benefit the Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation funding for type 1 diabetes research. 21-and-older show. E-mail eromero@jdrf.org for details and to make reservations. Tickets can be pre-ordered or purchased at the door.

location: 3 S. Second St., Suite 117 Phoenix, AZ, 85004
name: Rock to Cure
description: Enjoy a live line-up of local bands, including Dust Jacket, Snail Quail and Hunger Artists. This rock 'n roll show is organized by young adults with type 1 diabetes. Proceeds benefit the Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation. Tickets can be pre-ordered or purchased at the door.
