venue: Toby Keith’s I Love This Bar and Grill
description: These Mesa punk rockers burst into the national limelight with their 2002 debut, “A Passage In Time,” which showcased the band’s blend of reggae, Spanish rock and punk. The album spawned the hits “One More Minute” and “Over Seasons.” The group followed this early success with 2004’s “Andiamó,” which reached No. 24 on the Billboard Heatseekers chart, and 2007’s “12:34.” The band is currently touring in support of its fourth album, 2010’s “Stories of Survival.”

location: 16844 N. Arrowhead Fountains Center Drive Peoria, AZ, 85382
name: Paperback Writer -- The Beatles Tribute Show
description: Take a magical mystery tour back to the 1960s with this this top-notch tribute band. Acclaimed by the Los Angeles Times and the New York Times, Paperback Writer captures the looks and sounds of the Fab Four, from the "mop top" days on "The Ed Sullivan Show" through "Abbey Road." Showtimes at 6 and 8:30 p.m.

name: Flogging Molly
description: This seven-piece Celtic punk band from Los Angeles arrives behind its hard-driving fifth album, this year's "Speed of Darkness."

location: 41703 N. Gavilan Peak Parkway Anthem, AZ, 85086
name: Music in May Concert Series: The Rave
description: Performing as part of Anthem's Music in May Concert Series, Phoenix cover band the Rave performs its high-energy renditions of classic rock and roll hits. The group has been playing together since 1986, and has appeared at the P.F. Chang's Rock 'n' Roll Arizona Marathon.

name: Portugal. The Man
description: Originally from Wasilla, Alaska, these experimental, psychedelic indie-rockers have performed at Bonnaroo and Lollapalooza. They toured alongside HORSE the Band and Les Claypool. Known for their frenzied laser shows during performances, the band arrives behind its latest album, 2010's "American Ghetto." Rock bands Telekinesis and Unknown Mortal Orchestra open this all-ages show.

location: 16844 N. Arrowhead Fountains Center Drive Peoria, AZ, 85382
name: The Beach Toys: A Tribute to the Beach Boys
description: This tribute band brings the classic California surf rock sound and style of the Beach Boys to Skye Restaurant, performing hits such as "I Get Around," "Surfer Girl,""Surfin' USA" and "Help Me Rhonda." Showtimes at 4 and 7 p.m.

name: Coheed and Cambria
description: Combining elements of progressive rock, punk and heavy metal, these New York rockers have released five concept albums that chronicle a science-fiction storyline called "The Amory Wars." The group's latest album, 2010's "Year of the Black Rainbow," is a prequel to the storyline.

name: Affinity Jazz
description: This 10-piece band performs big band jazz hits and a variety of popular music, including hits by Frank Sinatra, Michael Buble, Santana, Sister Sledge and the Eagles.

name: Take Action Tour With Bayside and Silverstein
description: Punk bands Bayside and Silverstein lead this punk rock tour, which also features the Swellers, Polar Bear Club and Texas in July.

name: Man Man
description: Known for their extremely wild stage shows, these experimental Philadelphia indie-rockers dress in all-white outfits and apply war paint,. They also play a slew of unusual instruments. The group has toured with Modest Mouse and Yeasayer, and has performed at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival, All Tomorrow's Parties and Primavera Sound. The group arrives in support of its latest album, 2011's "Life Fantastic." Indie-rockers Shilpa Ray open this all-ages show.

name: Eisley
description: Made up of four siblings, this Texas indie-rock group arrives behind its third album, 2011's "The Valley." Rock bands the Narrative and Christie Dupree also perform at this all-ages show.

name: B/S - The Tribute to Bon Scott-era AC/DC
description: This Phoenix band pays tribute to the Bon Scott-era of AC/DC, re-creating the look and sound of the Australian metal legends 1979 live show. The band performs hits such as “High Voltage,” “Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap” and “It's a Long Way to the Top (If You Wanna Rock 'n' Roll).”

name: Concerts in the Park Series: Firefly
description: Sisters Melanie, McKenzie and Madelyn Merchan make up this country pop band. The group has opened for LeAnn Rimes, Carrie Underwood, the Zac Brown Band, and Justin Bieber. Gilbert singer-songwriter Anna Collins also performs at this all-ages show.

name: Symphony X
description: This New Jersey progressive metal band has earned a devoted following with its aggressive, technically difficult brand of symphonic metal. The band released its latest album, "Paradise Lost," in 2007, and is currently working on another album.

name: Alien Ant Farm
description: These southern California alternative rockers hit it big with their amped-up rendition of Micheal Jackson's "Smooth Criminal," which hit No. 1 on the Billboard Alternative Songs. After a series of breakups, the band has reunited with the original line up and a batch of new songs. Alien Ant Farm's most recent album, "Up in the Attic," was released in 2006.

name: Of Montreal
description: These Athens, Ga., indie-rockers started out as a jangly psychedelic rock band, but have since toyed with a number of genres, including electronica, funk and glam rock. Known for their increasingly elaborate stage shows, the band's new album, 2010's "False Priest," finds them exploring R&B sounds. It features appearances by Janelle Monáe and Solange Knowles.

location: 41703 N. Gavilan Peak Parkway Anthem, AZ, 85086
name: Music in May Concert Series: Mogollon
description: Performing as part of Anthem's Music in May Concert Series, this four-piece band performs its blend of guitar wizardry and dueling fiddles. The group was formed in Overgaard and is named for the area's distinct Mogollon Rim.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Joan of Arc
description: Led by singer-songwriter Tim Kinsella, formally of the influential emo band Cap'n Jazz, these Chicago indie-rockers create their scrappy songs from complex studio techniques and instrumental guitar work. The group arrives in support of its latest album, this year's "Life Like." Rock bands Air Waves and Knesset open this all-ages show.

name: Silhouette
description: This vibrant local band performs high-energy versions of classic R&B, soul, and Motown tunes. The group formed in 2005 and began playing at the Barcelona Restaurant in Scottsdale.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: The Black Angels
description: These scrappy Austin, Texas-based psychedelic indie-rockers have played Lollapalooza, South By Southwest and All Tomorrow's Parties. They have toured with the Black Keys, Black Rebel Motorcycle Club and the Brian Jonestown Massacre. The group's new album, 2010's "Phosphene Dream," hit No. 50 on the Billboard Top 200 chart. Indie-rockers Sleepy Sun open this all-ages show.

name: "Experience Hendrix"
description: This all-star tribute to guitar legend Jimi Hendrix features performances of some of his best songs by top guitarists, including Billy Cox of the Jimi Hendrix Experience, Steve Vai, Robert Randolph, David Hidalgo and Cesar Rosas, the North Mississippi All-Stars and Brad Whitford.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Voodoo Glow Skulls
description: These California punks have kept the flame of ska burning bright since 1988. The band has played with the Mighty Mighty Bosstones and the Slackers. They released their most recent album, "Southern California Street Music," in 2007. The band is currently working on a new album.

name: Danzig
description: Led by fiery frontman Glenn Danzig, former leader of horror punks the Misfits, these New Jersey heavy-metal rockers arrive in support of their ninth album, 2010's "Deth Red Sabaoth." The album hit No. 35 on the Billboard 200 chart, the highest-charting album for the band since 1994's "Danzig 4p." Metal bands DevilDriver and 2 Cents also perform at this all-ages show.

name: Brooke Fraser
description: This pop-folk singer-songwriter has earned a large following in her native New Zealand and has garnered an international fan base with her latest release, 2010's "Flags."

name: Kansas
description: These classic rockers scored hits in the 1970s with songs such as "Carry On Wayward Son" and "Dust in the Wind," landing them two multi-platinum albums and five gold albums. The group's latest album, "Somewhere to Elsewhere," marked the reunion of the band's original 1970s lineup.

name: Loren Battle
description: This Phoenix-based hardcore band has been winning over national audiences with its breakdown-heavy, metal-influenced brand of hardcore punk. The band has released two albums, “Words Begin Wars" and “Learning to Live With Open Wounds."

name: Joe Pug
description: This Chicago singer-songwriter has toured with Steve Earle, Josh Ritter and M. Ward. He arrives in support of his debut album, 2010's "Messenger." Indie-rockers Strand of Oaks and Tristen open this 21-and-older show.

name: White Denim
description: These scrappy garage rockers are known for their wild live shows, with jammy sections adding to the group's already unusual song structures. The group arrives in support of its latest record, 2010's "Last Day of Summer." Indie rockers St. Ranger open this all-ages show.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: John Vanderslice
description: This indie-rock singer-songwriter's adventurous pop tunes have made him a cult favorite since his debut album, 2000's "Mass Suicide Occult Figurines." Vanderslice has worked as a producer on albums by Spoon and the Mountain Goats. He released his most recent album, "White Wilderness," in 2011. Phoenix indie-rockers the Whisperlights open this all-ages show.

name: Mötley Crüe
description: These Los Angeles heavy metal legends return to the Valley, bringing songs from their 2008 record, "Saints of Los Angeles," the first album to feature the original lineup in more than a decade. Known for hit such as "Dr. Feelgood," "Shout at the Devil" and "Smokin' in the Boys Room," the band's hard-partying members have kept the group in the public eye, earning attention for brushedswith the law, drug problems and other tabloid fodder. Rock bands Poison and the New York Dolls open this all-ages show.

name: The Twilight Singers
description: Fronted by former Afghan Whigs leader Greg Dulli, these New Orleans indie-rockers perform the dark, moody songs from their latest release, 2011's "Dynamite Steps." The album earned an 8/10 reviews from Spin and a 7.9/10 from Pitchfork. Indie rockers Margot and the Nuclear So and Sos open this all-ages show.

name: Ted Nugent
description: Known as much for his outspoken conservative politics as his hard-driving rock songs, this Detroit guitar legend returns to the Valley as part of his I Still Believe Tour. Nugent has sold more than 30 million albums during his decades-long career, scoring hits such as "Stranglehold," "Free for All," "Dog Eat Dog" and "Cat Scratch Fever."

name: Cage The Elephant/Manchester Orchestra
description: Known for their high-energy show, Kentucky's Cage the Elephant's self-titled 2008 debut featured the hit singles "Ain't No Rest for the Wicked" and "In One Ear." The group's second album, "Thank You, Happy Birthday," hit No. 2 on the Billboard 200 charts. Georgia indie-rockers Manchester Orchestra perform songs from their latest record, 2011's "Simple Math," a follow-up to their successful sophomore release, 2009's "Mean Everything to Nothing." Indie-rockers Sleeper Agent open this all-ages show.

name: Cinderella
description: These Philadelphia glam rockers were a huge hit in the mid-1980s, with their first three albums going platinum and scoring hits such as "Nobody's Fool," "Don't Know What You Got (Till It's Gone)" and "Coming Home." The group arrives as part of its 25th Anniversary Tour. Rockers Sludge's Build a Band open this all-ages show.

name: Killing Joke
description: Formed in 1978, this English post-punk band blends metal, synth-rock and punk rock; the sound was influential on the genre of industrial rock. Killing Joke released their 14th album, "Absolute Dissent," in 2010, the group's first record in 28 years to feature the band's original lineup. Rock bands the Crying Spell and Indicator Dogz open this all-ages show.

name: Journey
description: These multi-platinum rock icons return to the Valley in support of their 2011 album, "Eclipse," the group's second with lead singer Arnel Pineda. The San Fransisco rockers hit their peak popularity in the 1970s and '80s, scoring two gold albums, eight multi-platinum albums, and one diamond record. Among their hits were "Open Arms,""When You Love a Woman" and "Don't Stop Believin'." Rock band Foreigner also performs at this all-ages show.

name: Def Leppard
description: These English heavy-metal legends return to the Valley, playing songs from throughout their career as well tunes from their new live album, 2011's "Mirrorball." Emerging as part of the new wave of British heavy metal movement of the late 1970s, Def Leppard scored radio hits such as "Love Bites," "Pour Some Sugar on Me" and "Photograph"; albums "Hysteria" and "Pyromania" have sold more than 10 million copies each. Seattle rock legends Heart also perform at this all-ages show.

name: The Noodles
description: Sunday afternoons, the Sail Inn plays home to this Grateful Dead tribute band. The Noodles play their improv heavy renditions of the Dead's best songs, attracting a faithful following of Deadheads.

name: Panic! at the Disco
description: These Las Vegas pop-punk rockers hit it big with their 2005 debut, "A Fever You Can't Sweat Out," which hit No. 13 on the Billboard 200 chart and went double platinum. The band moved toward a baroque pop style on its second album, 2008's "Pretty. Odd." Only lead singer Brendon Urie and drummer Spencer Smith remain in the group. The group's third album, 2011's "Vices & Virtues," hit No. 7 on the Billboard 200 chart. Rock bands Fun and Funeral Party open this all-ages show.

name: The Maine/Augustana
description: The second album by Tempe pop punks the Maine, 2010's "Black and White," debuted at No. 16 on the Billboard 200 chart, and the record won "Album of the Year 2010" in AP Magazine's Readers’ Awards. San Diego pop punks Augustana's third album, 2008's "Can't Love, Can't Hurt," hit No. 21 on the U.S. Billboard 200 chart, and the band arrives in support of its 2011 self-titled fourth album. Mesa singer-songwriter Austin Gibbs opens this all-ages show.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Black Lips
description: These Atlanta indie-punks have performed on "Late Night with Conan O'Brien," and played at South by Southwest and the Pitchfork Music Festival. Known for their outrageous stage show, inspired by the punk shows of GG Allin, the group arrives in support of its 2011 album, "Arabia Mountain." Hardcore punks Cerebral Ballzy open this all-ages show.

name: Dropkick Murphys
description: These Boston Celtic punks perform their high-energy blend of traditional Irish music and hardcore punk, playing songs from their seventh album, 2011's "Going Out in Style." The band has performed alongside Aerosmith and Bruce Springsteen, and its music was featured in the films "The Fighter" and "The Departed."

location: 7301 E. Indian Bend Road Scottsdale, AZ, 85250
name: Sunday Night Concert Series
description: On Sunday evenings, visitors are invited to sit on the grass and listen to a variety of local bands. Train and carousel rides are available. Train rides are $2 and carousel rides are $1, and age 3 and younger ride free with a paying adult. Food and beverages are available for purchase.

name: Chandler Symphony Orchestra
description: The Chandler Symphony Orchestra presents this chamber concert of humorous music, including the "Musical Joke" by W.A. Mozart, the "Farewell Symphony" by F.J. Haydn, and music by J. J. Grier, Bach, John Cage and Sergei Taneyev.

location: 25062 E. Meridian Road Queen Creek, AZ, 85242
name: "Music in the Grove"
description: Singers from the Phoenix Opera perform popular and operatic works, while visitors sample culinary dishes and fine wine from the Queen Creek Olive Mill.

location: 700 W. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Performance with A View: The ASU Herberger String Quartet
description: The ASU Herberger String Quartet, under the direction of ASU School of Music violist Nancy Buck, perform a free concert of classical works. Presented by the Friends of the Tempe Center for the Arts.

name: Pancake Run
venue: Riparian Preserve at Water Ranch Lake
description: Work up an appetite and eat pancakes after your 10km Run or 5km Run/Walk. Enjoy classical music by orchestra students. Participants are automatically entered into a raffle. Proceeds benefit the Gilbert Orchestra Club. To sponsor a student, where a portion of the proceeds goes directly to the student, write in the name when registering.

name: North Valley Chorale: "Peace Offerings"
description: The chorale performs its final concert of the season, singing "Dona Nobis Pacem" by Vaughan Williams, accompanied by psalms, songs and poems of peace.

name: "Maestros in Concert: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma and Zakir Hussain"
description: Internationally recognized and award-winning Indian artists Pandit Shivkumar Sharma and Zakir Hussain perform classical music of India.

name: "Mother's Day at the Opera"
description: Celebrate Mother's Day with operatic selections courtesy of the Symphony of Southwest.

name: Kronos Quartet
description: The Kronos Quartet is recognized worldwide for expanding the accepted range and context of the string quartet through exploration and experimentation. They have become an influential group in the chamber music industry.

name: Arizona Women in Tune Concert
description: The Arizona Women in Tune chorus presents "Zip, Zing and Zessst," a high-spirited concert of lively songs and colorful performances.

name: Concert Benefiting Leader Dogs for the Blind
description: Concert pianist Duncan Holmes performs. Holmes is a recipient of a Leader Dog. For details, e-mail lorifroelich@gmail.com.

name: Sun and Song Outdoor Music Series: Gabriel Ayala
price: $5, $4 age 65 and older, $2 ages 6-12 and students with ID, free members, American Indians and age 6 and younger
description: This Pascua Yaqui guitarist is one of the leaders of a new movement of Native Americans establishing professional careers performing classical music. Ayala has toured nationally. Free with museum admission.

name: Art Inspires Art
price: $10, $8 age 65 and older and students with valid ID, $4 ages 6-12, free age 5 and younger and museum members
description: Students from Arizona State University School of Music responded to “Guillotine of Sunlight, Guillotine of Shade” by artist Peter Wegner with original works for a string quartet. This is the fifth year of this collaboration.

name: Jeordie
description: Blending modern pop tunes with folk guitar, this Phoenix singer-songwriter has performed as a supporting act for Dido, Jewel, Indigo Girls, Sade and Brooks & Dunn. She also recently released a 23-track live album called "Bootleg."

name: Hogjaw European Tour Kick-off
description: This Arizona band plays to the strengths of their desert home, crafting alt-country tunes packed with dusty tails and fiery energy. The band released its latest album, “Ironwood," in 2010. Their European tour includes stops in Norway, the Czech Republic, France and Spain. Local rock bands Cogswell, Boy Named Sioux and Dagg Nabbit Stubbs also perform at this 21-and-older show.

name: Hans Olson
description: This Valley blues legend performs his blend of old-school blues, classic country and folk music, playing songs from his 17 albums. Olson has played a major role in the Valley music scene for decades, helping to found the now-defunct Sun Club in 1986, a Tempe hot spot that helped launch the careers of bands like Dead Hot Workshop and the Gin Blossoms. He also helped establish the Phoenix Blues Society, the Arizona Blues Hall of Fame and the Arizona Music and Entertainment Hall of Fame. Olson has toured the U.S. and Europe several times. His music appears in a number of movies and television shows, including "Cold Case," "Ghost Whisperer," "Criminal Minds" and "It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia." Performing on the AMC Fountain stage.

location: 16844 N. Arrowhead Fountains Center Drive Peoria, AZ, 85382
name: Bo Bice
description: This Alabama singer-songwriter rose to fame after taking home second place on the fourth season of "American Idol," losing the top spot to Carrie Underwood. Bice arrives behind his third album, 2010's "3."

location: 2000 E. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Jeordie
description: Blending modern pop tunes with folk guitar, this Phoenix singer-songwriter has performed as a supporting act for Dido, Jewel, Indigo Girls, Sade and Brooks & Dunn. She also recently released a 23-track live album called "Bootleg."

name: Kenny Chesney
description: This country music superstar returns to the Valley in support of his latest album, 2010's "Hemingway's Whiskey." The album, which debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 chart, is Chesney's sixth No. 1 album, placing him just behind Garth Brooks for the most No. 1 albums by a country artist. Combing his country sound with a laid-back beach vibe, Chesney has earned eight platinum albums and three gold records. Country singers Billy Currington and Uncle Kracker also perform at this all-ages show.

name: Loretta Lynn
description: This Kentucky-born country music legend has landed 16 No. 1 country hits during her decadeslong career and influenced a generation of musicians. Known for songs such as "Don't Come Home A' Drinkin' (With Lovin' on Your Mind)," "Fist City" and "Woman of the World (Leave My World Alone)," Lynn also wrote a 1976 autobiography,"Coal Miner's Daughter," which was made into the 1980 Academy Award-winning film of the same name, starring Sissy Spacek and Tommy Lee Jones. In 2004, Lynn teamed with Jack White of the White Stripes for her Grammy Award-winning album "Van Lear Rose," which reached No. 2 on the Billboard Top Country Albums chart. The tribute album "Coal Miner's Daughter: A Tribute to Loretta Lynn" was released in 2010, featuring performances by top artists such as Gretchen Wilson, Alan Jackson, Paramore, the White Stripes, Kid Rock and Lucinda Williams.

name: Leon Russell
description: Inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame this year, this celebrated Oklahoma-born singer-songwriter arrives behind his latest release, 2010's "The Union," a collaboration with Elton John. Russell began his career as a session musician, playing with artists such as Jerry Lee Lewis, George Harrison, Eric Clapton, the Beach Boys and Willie Nelson. He's written hit songs performed by artists such as Ray Charles, B.B. King and Joe Cocker. Russell enjoyed success with his own hits such as "Tight Rope" and "Lady Blue."

name: The Reverend Horton Heat
description: Guitarist Jim Heath leads this psychobilly rock band, playing an amp-ed up blend of country, punk, swing and rockabilly. The group has been an underground favorite for nearly two decades, and it arrives in support of its latest record, 2009's "Laughin' & Cryin' with the Reverend Horton Heat." Rockabilly band the Swingin' Utters open this all-ages show.

name: Cinco de Mayo Salsa Festival
price: Free salsa and tequila samples, food and beverage prices vary
description: Sample salsas from more than a dozen Arizona chefs and restaurants competing for the title of best salsa in the Valley. Free tequila tastings are offered. Also available are mexican desserts, beverages and grilled tacos al carbon and tostada de carnitas. The Freddie Duran Plan band plays Latin, jazz and American hits. ABC 15’s Andi Barness from "Sonoran Living Live" emcees. Sponsored by Chamucos Tequila.

location: 2000 E. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Hans Olson
description: This Valley blues legend performs his blend of old-school blues, classic country and folk music, playing songs from his 17 albums. Olson has played a major role in the Valley music scene for decades, helping to found the now-defunct Sun Club in 1986, a Tempe hot spot that helped launched the careers of band like Dead Hot Workshop and the Gin Blossoms. He also helped to establish the Phoenix Blues Society, the Arizona Blues Hall of Fame and the Arizona Music and Entertainment Hall of Fame. Olson has toured the U.S. and Europe several times, and his music also appears in a number of movies and television shows, including "Cold Case," "Ghost Whisperer," "Criminal Minds" and "It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia."

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Big Nick and the Gila Monsters
description: This local blues band has been together since 1993, impressing Valley blues fans with a rocking blues sound and Big Nick Riviera's soulful vocals. A member of the Arizona Blues Hall of Fame, the group recently released a double CD called "Shakin', Not Stirred" and "Working Without a Net."

location: 700 W. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Songwriters' Showcase V
description: This showcase features local musicians who have participated in the Tempe Center for the Arts' weekly Walk-in Wednesdays Open Mic series. The show is headlined by local guitarist William Eaton, who performs on his hand-built instruments. Eaton has been a longtime collaborator with Native American flutist R. Carlos Nakai. Their album, 2001's "In A Distant Place," was nominated for a Grammy for "Best New Age Album."

name: Jazz on the Promenade Series: Cold Shott and the Hurricane Horns
description: This eight-piece Arizona R&B band has been performing together for more than 20 years, gaining a reputation for funky, high-energy stage shows. The group released a live album, "If You Got the Blues...," in 2003. This event also features wine tastings and specialty food sampling for an extra charge, with proceeds going to the non-profit group City of Hope, which works to fight cancer, diabetes, HIV/AIDS and other life-threatening diseases.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Rhythm Room All-Stars
description: Celebrate the blues with some of the top players in town. Founded by harmonica player and Rhythm Room owner Bob Corritore in 1991, the group features Chris James on guitar, Patrick Rynn on bass and Brian Fahey on drums, playing their brand of Chicago blues. The band has opened for B.B. King and toured Europe, performing songs off its album, "I'm Here Baby."

location: 7000 E. Mayo Blvd., Suite 21 Phoenix, AZ, 85054
name: McDowell Mountain Music Festival
description: This annual music festival returns to the Compound Grill for the second year in a row, bringing a batch of indie favorites, jam bands and world music groups. This year's festival is headlined by hippie indie-folk rockers Edward Sharpe and the Magnetic Zeros and blues rockers Black Joe Lewis and the Honeybears. The lineup also includes performances by JJ Grey and Mofro, SOJA, Xavier Rudd and the Otis Taylor Band. Proceeds benefit Ear Candy, a non-profit music education organization, and Phoenix Day, an organization that works with early education programs.

name: Music in the Garden: Big Nick and the Gila Monsters
description: This local blues band has been together since 1993, impressing Valley fans with their rocking blues sound and Big Nick Riviera soulful vocals. Members of the Arizona Blues Hall of Fame, the group recently released a double CD called "Shakin', Not Stirred" and "Working Without a Net." This popular event also features a chef-attended food station featuring weekly specials for an additional charge and a cash bar. A 21-and-older event.

name: Jazz on the Promenade Series: The DelRayz
description: This Phoenix blues band is the latest musical endeavor for local blueswomen Rochelle Raya and Nancy Dalessandro, who have been playing Valley clubs for nearly two decades. The group performs a mix of classic covers and soul-infused originals. This event also features wine tastings and specialty food sampling for an extra charge.Proceeds go to the non-profit group City of Hope, which works to fight against cancer, diabetes, HIV/AIDS and other life-threatening diseases.

name: Curse of the Pink Hearse
description: Lead by outlandish bassist Marco Polo, this Phoenix band blends its high-energy psychobilly with strong Mexican influences. Polo also creates the soundtracks for his spy-flavored films, including his "The Ghetto Was Never Enough."

name: Mother’s Day Jazz Brunch
description: Celebrate with the music of the Great Ladies of Jazz, featuring local divas Margo Reed, Nancy Gee, Sherry Roberson and Delphine Cortez. The four singers perform a host of classic jazz and songs from the Great American Songbook. Brunch buffet is provided by Fabulous Food Fine Catering and Events. A cash bar is available and a complimentary rose is presented to mothers.

name: Brian McKnight
description: This R&B crooner performs his smooth songs, including hits such as "Back at One," "Love Is" and "You Should Be Mine (Don't Waste Your Time)." McKnight appeared in the second season of Celebrity Apprentice in 2009, and hosts his own late night talk show, "The Brian McKnight Show." His latest album, 2009's "Evolution of a Man," hit No. 3 on the US R&B charts.

name: Sunorus
description: This Phoenix quintet has become a staple of the Valley jazz scene, playing an experimental blend of neo-traditional jazz, funk and rock, drawing comparisons to groups like Tortoise. This show is the release party for the group's new album, "Greenhouse."

name: Sun and Song Outdoor Music Series: Manny Perez
price: $5, $4 age 65 and older, $2 ages 6-12 and students with ID, free members, American Indians and age 6 and younger
description: This budding Pascua Yaqui guitarist presents an assortment of genres and dynamic styles. He feeds off audience energy and response, so the more the crowd gives the more he gives back. Free with museum admission.

name: Jazz on the Promenade Series: Groove Merchants
description: This high-energy cover band takes on songs by everyone from Stevie Wonder to Maroon 5. This event also features wine tastings and specialty food samplings for an extra charge. Proceeds go to the non-profit group City of Hope, which works to fight against cancer, diabetes, HIV/AIDS and other life-threatening diseases.

location: 7000 E. Mayo Blvd., Suite 21 Phoenix, AZ, 85054
name: Jimmy Warren
description: This acclaimed blues-rock guitarist arrives behind his third album, released earlier this year. Warren's brand of edgy, blues rock has been described as a cross among Eric Clapton, George Benson and Jimi Hendrix.

name: Music in the Garden: Bad Cactus Brass Band
description: This New Orleans-style street jazz band fis powered tuba, drums, trumpets, saxophones and trombones. The band takes on funky dance numbers, street beats, traditional Dixieland and swing, and reinvented versions of modern pop tunes with all the energy of a Mardi Gras celebration. The band recorded its first album, 2010’s “Arizona Mardi Gras,” live at the Lost Leaf bar in downtown Phoenix. This popular event also features a chef-attended food station featuring weekly specials for an additional charge, along with a cash bar. A 21-and-older event.

name: Jazz on the Promenade Series: Nicole Pesce
description: This celebrated Phoenix pianist spent many years in residence at the central Phoenix restaurant My Florist and the Ritz Carton Hotel, winning over diners with her virtuosic piano playing. With more than 500 songs committed to memory, Pesce plays everything from Gershwin to John Mayer. She’s performed with Jerry Lewis, Debbie Reynolds and Pat Boone, and performed special concerts for Shaquille O’Neal, Janet Napolitano and President George H.W. Bush. This event also features wine tastings and specialty food sampling for an additional charge, with proceeds going to the non-profit group City of Hope, which works to fight against cancer, diabetes, HIV/AIDS and other life-threatening diseases.

location: 41703 N. Gavilan Peak Parkway Anthem, AZ, 85086
name: Music in May Concert Series: Lucius Parr and Street Life
description: This local rhythm-and-blues band has performing together for more than 15 years. Band leader Lucius Parr has been playing his smooth, old-school R&B sounds around the Valley since 1968, and has opened for such artists such as B.B. King and Charlie Daniels.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Dirty Dozen Brass Band
description: This New Orleans brass band has been playing together since 1977, performing their influential blend of traditional New Orleans-style, and funk and bebop jazz. The group has worked with a diverse lineup of artists, including Elvis Costello, Modest Mouse, Norah Jones, Dizzy Gillespie and Branford Marsalis. The group is touring in celebration of the remastered release of its debut album, 1984's "My Feet Can't Fail Me Now." A 21-and-older show.

name: William Fitzsimmons
description: The gentle folk-rock tunes by this Illinois-based singer-songwriter have appeared on the TV series "Grey's Anatomy," "Brothers & Sisters," "Life of Ryan" and "One Tree Hill." Fitzsimmons released his latest album, "Derivatives," in 2010. Indie-rockers Slow Runners open this all-ages show.

name: The Low Anthem
description: These Rhode Island indie-rockers have performed their folk-rock tunes at Bonnaroo, Lollapalloza, the Newport Folk Festival and Austin City Limits. They have also performed on "The Late Show with David Letterman." The band arrives in support of their new album, 2011's "Smart Flesh."

name: The Rhythm Ramblers
description: This 18-piece Sun City big band performs classic hits from the big band era, joined by singers Marge Nelson and Kent Parry. This dance is held the first Tuesday of each month.

name: Sade
description: Led by lead vocalist Sade Adu, this English R&B band has sold more than 50 million albums worldwide since its multi-platinum debut, 1984's "Diamond Life." Maintaining a smooth, soulful sound, the group released "Soldier of Love" in 2010, the group's first original album for a decade. The album debuted at No. 1 on the U.S. Billboard 200 chart and won the Grammy for best R&B performance by a duo or group with vocals. Soul singer John Legend opens this all-ages show.

location: The Buttes 2000 Westcourt Way Tempe, AZ, 85282
name: Chuck E. Baby and the All Stars
description: This local band rocks this resort bar every Saturday night, performing a range of classic rock tunes, blues track and original songs. Songs off the group's first album, "Never in a Million Years," were picked up by MTV and used in several episodes of the hit series "The Real World."

location: 10455 E. Pinnacle Peak Parkway Scottsdale, AZ, 85255
name: Mosaico
description: This Arizona flamenco group performs original music inspired by the sounds of Spain, Latin America and the Caribbean. Incorporating guitar, bass, flute, violin, piano and percussion, the group adds a taste of the Southwest to their performance.

name: Freddie Duran Plan
description: Lead by longtime Valley songwriter Freddie Duran, this local band performs its mix of Latin jazz, Tejano and rock tunes, and original songs.

name: "Jazz Con Alma"
description: Celebrate Cinco de Mayo with pianist Beth Lederman as she performs an evening of salsa, samba, Latin jazz and standards.

location: 9800 E. Indian Bend Road Salt River Reservation, AZ, 85256
name: Los Lobos
description: These Grammy Award-winning Chicano rockers have been a fan favorite since their major label debut, 1984's "How Will the Wolf Survive?." Combining elements of Tex-Mex blues and rock and roll with traditional Spanish and Mexican music styles, the band has remained a critical and commercial darling. The band's latest effort, 2010's "Tin Can Trust," was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Americana Album. A 21-and-older event.

name: Music in the Garden: Cosmos
description: This Valley band performs its energetic brand of Greek and Mediterranean fusion music, performed on traditional instruments. The group is currently working on its debut album. This popular event also features a chef-attended food station featuring weekly specials for an additional charge and a cash bar. A 21-and-older event.

name: Salsa Festival
description: Costa Rican orchestra Son de Tikizia and Colombia's Carolina La O perform salsa music. Dance shows feature national and Arizona talent. DJs play salsa, mambo and bachata music. teaches participants salsa and bachata dances. An 18-and-older event.

name: Steel Pulse
description: Led by singer-songwriter David Hinds, this influential roots-reggae group from Birmingham, England, has been together since 1975. They are known for their outspoken Rastafarian politics and fiery music. The group won a Grammy for their 1986 album, "Babylon the Bandit," and released their latest album, "African Holocaust," in 2004. Steel Pulse are currently working on their next record, and recently released the song "Hold On 4 Haiti," with proceeds going to earthquake relief in Haiti.

name: Lil Wayne
description: This Grammy Award-winning rapper returns to the Valley behind his eighth album, 2010's "I Am Not a Human Being," which debuted at No. 2 on the US Billboard 200 chart. The tour is Lil Wayne's first major tour since serving an eight-month prison sentence in New York, and "I Am Not a Human Being" is his hip-hop follow-up to his multi-platinum 2008 breakthrough, "Tha Carter III." Lil Wayne recently released his new single, "6 Foot 7 Foot," the first song off his heavily anticipated "The Carter IV" album, slated to be released this year. Rappers Nicki Minaj, Rick Ross and Travis Barker and Mixmaster Mike also perform at this all-ages show.

name: The Digitour 2011
description: This tour brings together artists who gained national exposure through YouTube videos. The show features performances by David Days, the Gregory Brothers, David Choi, Destorm, Mystery Guitar Man and Ricky Ficarelli.

location: 20000 S. Maricopa Road Gila River Reservation, AZ, 85226
name: Xtreme Drift Circuit Concert and Car Show
description: This annual show combines hot custom cars and live music. The show features performances by hip-hop artists Jeremih and Mann, and other Def Jam artists. The show also offers displays of custom cars, bikes and trucks.

name: Bone Thugs-n-Harmony
description: This influential gangster rap group arrives behind its eighth album, 2010's "Uni5: The World's Enemy," which debuted on No. 14 on the Billboard 200 chart. The group help establish the gangster rap genre in the early 1990s, starting with their 1994 record, "Creepin on ah Come Up."

location: 2000 E. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Cold Shott and the Hurricane Horns
description: This eight-piece Arizona R&B band has been performing together for more than 20 years, gaining a reputation for their funky, high-energy stage shows. The group released a live album, "If You Got the Blues ...," in 2003.

location: 2000 E. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Knee Deep Experience
description: Led by Rochester, N.Y., native Chris Brown, this local five-piece band sports a classic funk sound, drawing inspiration from funk pioneer George Clinton. The band performs cover songs as well as original works from its albums, “Funkigula” and "Dr. Zaius.” Performing on the District Stage.

name: Open Mic Night
description: This downtown Phoenix coffeehouse welcomes local musicians, performance artists and poets to this weekly, all-acoustic open mic night. All genres and styles welcome, with mics and amps provided. Hosted by James Claymon and Jason Lynn

name: HipHop Benefit Show: Supporting Japan
description: Entertainers include Steffen, KT Cool, Fiyah Station and Bobby BrandNew. Raffle prizes include items donated by cLorae.baca.photography, Pink House Boutique in Glendale, From Another Planet apparel in Phoenix and Bri Bridge in Glendale. Proceeds benefit the proceeds for the American Red Cross.

name: Rock the Zoo
description: Sample beverages from more than 30 wineries, breweries and national distributors. Barry Sobel perform a comedy routine. Music featuring sounds from the '80s is performed by a variety of bands, including Animotion, the Motels, Dramarama, Tommy Tutone and the Promise. A Rockin' Raffle is held for a cash prize. Attendees are encouraged to dress in '80s garb. A 21-and-older event. Ticket purchase includes a souvenir beer mug and liquor sample punch card. Additional VIP ticket details available online. Advance ticket purchase required.

location: 2000 E. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Dream State
description: These Mesa rockers create pop-rock songs filled with loud guitars and clever lyrics, taking cues from Smashing Pumpkins, Weezer and Jimmy Eat World. The band has performed at the Taste of Chaos show, playing songs from its album, “A Place to Rest My Head."

name: Xtra Ticket
description: Thursday nights, jam out to the songs of the Grateful Dead with Tempe tribute band Xtra Ticket. Each character in the group, which has been together since 1994, takes on a character from the Grateful Dead, creating faithful re-creations of some of the band's most iconic songs.

location: 7330 N. Dreamy Draw Drive Phoenix, AZ, 85020
name: Friday Night Live Music
description: This tucked-away Phoenix bar attracts a huge crowd on Friday nights and showcases a live bands on its outdoor patios. The schedule rotates each week and includes local rock bands Chris Parker Project, Zimis and North. Check Web site for updated schedule.

name: Alison Krauss
description: This Illinois-born bluegrass-country singer, songwriter and fiddler arrives in support of her latest record, this year's "Paper Airplane," the followup to her Grammy-winning 2007 album, "Raising Sand," a collaboration album with Led Zeppelin's Robert Plant. Krauss has won 26 Grammy Awards over the course of her career, making her the most honored female artist in Grammy history.

location: 5700 W. North Loop Road Gila River Reservation, AZ, 85226
name: Steve Barker Band
description: Led by singer Steve Barker, this Phoenix band performs traditional country tunes and classic Western songs. The group has released two albums, "20 Classic Songs" and "The Last Cowboy Song," and performs at Rawhide every week.

name: Wiz Khalifa
description: This Pittsburgh rapper arrives behind his debut studio album, 2011's "Rolling Papers." The album spawned the hit single, "Black and Yellow," which hit No. 1 on the Billboard chart. Rappers Big Sean and Chevy Woods also perform at this all-ages show.

location: 5734 E. Rancho Manana Blvd. Cave Creek, AZ, 85331
name: Sonoran Stars
description: The benefit begins with a cocktail hour and a silent auction, followed by the release of a rehabilitated raptor. Dinner is served and entertainment is by the Bar J Wranglers, a classic Western band of “singing cowboys.” The event also features a live auction after dinner. Guests are encouraged to dress in casual or Western wear, and to anticipate cool evening temperatures. Proceeds go to the Desert Foothills Land Trust, which acquires and cares for some of the community’s natural areas. Shuttle service begins at 5:15 p.m. from 38400 N. Schoolhouse Road, Cave Creek.

location: 5700 W. North Loop Road Gila River Reservation, AZ, 85226
name: Sundown Cookout
description: Take a mule-drawn hay-wagon ride at 6 p.m., and then dine outdoors. Options include barbecue chicken, T-bone steak, flat-iron steak and baby-back pork ribs. Sides include cowboy beans, baked potato, bread and warm apple pie. A kids menu and vegetarian options are available. After dinner, country music is performed and there is dancing under the stars. Other activities include marshmallow roast, cowboy storytelling and games. A cash bar is available. Pre-paid reservations required 48 hours in advance.

name: A Boy Named Sioux
description: Led by Rob Toner, this Tempe band blends outlaw country with elements of Southern rock and Southwestern twists, resulting in a sound somewhere between Waylon Jennings and Roger Clyne. The group performs tunes from their debut EP, "The Next Big Thing."

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Dirty Vegas
description: This British house music trio hit it big with its 2001 single "Days Go By," which first hit the mainstream after being featured in a commercial for the 2003 Mitsubishi Eclipse. The song hit No. 14 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 chart and earned the group a Grammy for Best Dance Recording. The group was on hiatus for many years, but released its first album in seven years, "Electric Love," this year. A 21-and-older show.

name: Jesse Cook
venue: Scottsdale Center for the Performing Arts
description: Juno Award-winning musician Jesse Cook has traveled the globe absorbing sounds from cultures of Spain, Africa, Cuba, Egypt, France and Brazil. His exotic rumba flamenco is a fusion of these musical traditions. His latest album, "The Rumba Foundation," features Latin rhythms inspired by a journey to Bogota, Colombia.

name: Cinco de Mayo Celebration
description: Get a free autograph of Marvel Comics' Spider-Man or have your picture taken with the popular hero for a fee. A Hispanic band and Ballet Folkloria perform. Kids can also take a free swing at candy-filled pinatas. Rides include a train and bumper boats, and there is a splash playground.

name: "Jazz Con Alma"
description: Celebrate with pianist Beth Lederman as she performs an evening of salsa, samba, Latin jazz and standards.

name: Cinco de Mayo 7th Anniversary Bash
description: The restaurant celebrates its seventh anniversary on May 5 with $3.50 margaritas and 1800 Tequila samples. Giveaways from beverage companies are featured. Revelers can dance to the music of Latin salsa band Projecto Clave beginning at 7 p.m. Cuisine options include clams Corona and salmon enchiladas.

name: Cinco de Mayo Music Festival & Raffle
Cinco de Mayo
description: Mex and Match food specials, normally $8.99, include tacos, enchiladas, tamales, burros, tostadas or chile rellenos and two side choices of Mexican rice, black beans, refried beans, vegetables or a cup of soup. Drink specials include $2 for Coors Light bottles or drafts, $3 for Corona, Corona Light or Pacifico and $5 for a 16-ounce Margarita de Macayo. Mariachis perform from 6 to 8 p.m.

name: Cinco de Mayo
description: Mex and Match food specials, normally $8.99, include tacos, enchiladas, tamales, burros, tostadas or chile rellenos and two side choices of Mexican rice, black beans, refried beans, vegetables or a cup of soup. Drink specials include $2 for Coors Light bottles or drafts, $3 for Corona, Corona Light or Pacifico and $5 for a 16-ounce Margarita de Macayo. Featured are face painting and mariachis from 5 to 8 p.m.

name: Cinco de Mayo
description: Mex and Match food specials, normally $8.99, include tacos, enchiladas, tamales, burros, tostadas or chile rellenos and two side choices of Mexican rice, black beans, refried beans, vegetables or a cup of soup. Drink specials include $2 for Coors Light bottles or drafts, $3 for Corona, Corona Light or Pacifico and $5 for a 16-ounce Margarita de Macayo. Featured are face painting from 5 to 8 p.m. and karaoke and live music from 5 to 10 p.m.

name: Cinco de Mayo
description: Mex and Match food specials, normally $8.99, include tacos, enchiladas, tamales, burros, tostadas or chile rellenos and two side choices of Mexican rice, black beans, refried beans, vegetables or a cup of soup. Drink specials include $2 for Coors Light bottles or drafts, $3 for Corona, Corona Light or Pacifico and $5 for a 16-ounce Margarita de Macayo. Featured are face painting from 4 to 7 p.m. and mariachis and a balloon artist from 5 to 8 p.m.

name: Cinco de Mayo
description: Mex and Match food specials, normally $8.99, include tacos, enchiladas, tamales, burros, tostadas or chile rellenos and two side choices of Mexican rice, black beans, refried beans, vegetables or a cup of soup. Drink specials include $2 for Coors Light bottles or drafts, $3 for Corona, Corona Light or Pacifico and $5 for a 16-ounce Margarita de Macayo. Featured are face painting and mariachis from 5 to 8 p.m., and karaoke from 5:30 to 10 p.m.

location: 8220 N. Hayden Road, Suite C111 Scottsdale, AZ, 85258
name: Cinco de Mayo Celebration
description: Live mariachi music is featured, a spotted donkey is available for petting and photographs, and Mexican cuisine and drink specials are offered. Order a chimichanga made with roasted chicken or stuffed peppers and add a $2 beer or $4 margarita, or get a Donkey Kick, a specialty drink made with habañero-infused tequila.

name: Cinco de Mayo Festival & Chihuahua Races

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Royal Bangs
description: These Knoxville indie-rockers were discovered on MySpace by Black Keys drummer Patrick Carney and quickly signed to his Audio Eagle Records label. With a sound that combines garage rock and modern indie rock, the group arrives in support of its second album, 2009's "Let It Beep." Indie-rockers Superhumanoids open this all-ages show.

name: Balance and Composure
description: These Pennsylvania punk rockers arrive in support of their latest album, 2009's "Only Boundaries," and their 2010 self-titled EP. Punk rockers the Riveras open this all-ages show.

location: 1019 E. Indian School Road Phoenix, AZ, 85014
name: Crystal Stilts
description: These New York City noise rockers perform the brooding songs from their latest album, 2011's "In Love With Oblivion," the follow-up to their critically acclaimed debut, 2008's "Alight of Night."

name: Cloudland Canyon
description: Combining the experimental electronic sounds of Kraftwerk with shoegazing psychedelic rock, these Georgia indie-rockers arrive in support of their 2010 album "Fin Eaves." A 21-and-older show.

name: The Dirty Heads
description: Playing the laid-back blend of reggae and ska pioneered by bands like Sublime, these mellow Southern California rockers have toured with O.A.R., 311, Pepper and the Kottonmouth Kings. The group released its debut album, "Any Port in a Storm," in 2008.

name: Terror
description: These Los Angeles hardcore punks are popular in the underground punk scene, and are known for their wild live shows. The group released its latest album, "Keepers Of the Faith," in 2010. Hardcore punk bands Stick To Your Guns, Trapped Under Ice, Close Your Eyes and Your Demise also perform at this all-ages show.

name: Authority Zero
venue: Toby Keith’s I Love This Bar and Grill
description: These Mesa punk rockers burst into the national limelight with their 2002 debut, “A Passage In Time,” which showcased the band’s blend of reggae, Spanish rock and punk. The album spawned the hits “One More Minute” and “Over Seasons.” The group followed this early success with 2004’s “Andiamó,” which reached No. 24 on the Billboard Heatseekers chart, and 2007’s “12:34.” The band is currently touring in support of its fourth album, 2010’s “Stories of Survival.”

name: Flogging Molly
description: This seven-piece Celtic punk band from Los Angeles arrives behind its hard-driving fifth album, this year's "Speed of Darkness."

name: Battle of the Bands – Winners Concert
description: The battle is over. Come hear the bands that were victorious over the competition. The concert is held in the college's Center for Performing Arts.

location: 41703 N. Gavilan Peak Parkway Anthem, AZ, 85086
name: Music in May Concert Series: The Rave
description: Performing as part of Anthem's Music in May Concert Series, Phoenix cover band the Rave performs its high-energy renditions of classic rock and roll hits. The group has been playing together since 1986, and has appeared at the P.F. Chang's Rock 'n' Roll Arizona Marathon.

name: Portugal. The Man
description: Originally from Wasilla, Alaska, these experimental, psychedelic indie-rockers have performed at Bonnaroo and Lollapalooza. They toured alongside HORSE the Band and Les Claypool. Known for their frenzied laser shows during performances, the band arrives behind its latest album, 2010's "American Ghetto." Rock bands Telekinesis and Unknown Mortal Orchestra open this all-ages show.

name: Coheed and Cambria
description: Combining elements of progressive rock, punk and heavy metal, these New York rockers have released five concept albums that chronicle a science-fiction storyline called "The Amory Wars." The group's latest album, 2010's "Year of the Black Rainbow," is a prequel to the storyline.

name: Take Action Tour With Bayside and Silverstein
description: Punk bands Bayside and Silverstein lead this punk rock tour, which also features the Swellers, Polar Bear Club and Texas in July.

name: Rachmaninoff's "All Night Vigil"
description: Riznica Chamber Choir performs Rachmaninoff's piece, which includes choral movements from the Orthodox Vesper service and from the Orthodox Matins service. Arrive 30-minutes early for a lecture on Orthodox music, presented by Lazo Mihajlovich, St. Sava Church choir director.

name: Kyle Phalen
description: Performing songs from his 2007 self-titled record and his debut, "I'll Be Ready," this Phoenix singer-songwriter's soulful acoustic songs have been compared to John Mayer and Gavin Degraw. Phalen performs a free acoustic set Saturday nights.

name: Meat Puppet
description: These celebrated Phoenix rockers, founded by brothers Curt and Cris Kirkwood, play a blend of punk rock, country and psychedelic rock. After the Kirkwood brothers served as guest musicians on Nirvana's "MTV Unplugged" performance in 1993, the Meat Puppet's 1994 album, "Too High to Die," hit No. 1 on the Billboard Heatseekers chart. The group broke up twice, but reunited in 2006. They are touring in support of their latest album, this year's "Lollipop."

location: 3900 E. Stanford Drive Paradise Valley, AZ, 85253
name: Orpheus Male Chorus: "Water in the Desert"
description: The Orpheus Male Chorus presents this water-themed concert, which features secular and sacred works, sea shanties and songs about pirates and mermaids. Call for prices.

name: Dropkick Murphys
description: These Boston Celtic punks perform their high-energy blend of traditional Irish music and hardcore punk, playing songs from their seventh album, 2011's "Going Out in Style." The band has performed alongside Aerosmith and Bruce Springsteen, and its music was featured in the films "The Fighter" and "The Departed."

name: Salt River Brass: "Rags to Riches"
description: Pianist Rich Ridenour joins the Salt River Brass for a concert dedicated to the music of the piano. The afternoon includes Scott Joplin’s "Maple Leaf Rag," Elton John’s "Funeral for a Friend," Claude Debussy’s "Claire de Lune" and finally George Gershwin's "Rhapsody in Blue."

location: 7301 E. Indian Bend Road Scottsdale, AZ, 85250
name: Sunday Night Concert Series
description: On Sunday evenings, visitors are invited to sit on the grass and listen to a variety of local bands. Train and carousel rides are available. Train rides are $2 and carousel rides are $1, and age 3 and younger ride free with a paying adult. Food and beverages are available for purchase.

name: Chandler Symphony Orchestra Chamber Concert: Arizona Composers
description: Families can experience orchestral music featuring a concerto for viola, clarinet and orchestra by Max Bruch, with Daniel Coombs on clarinet and Dwight Lear on viola. Other selections include Aram Khachaturian’s Suite No. 3 from “Gayane” and variations on an original theme for orchestra, “Enigma,” by Edward Elgar.

location: 9535 E. Riggs Road Sun Lakes, AZ, 85248
name: The East Valley Chorale
venue: First Baptist Church of Sun Lakes
description: The East Valley Chorale composed of singers from 35 churches throughout the state presents a concert featuring a variety of choral music. (Photo courtesy of the East Valley Chorale)

name: Carolyn Eynon Singers: "Songs of the American Spirit"
description: The group closes their 2010-11 season with a celebration of American composers and arrangers, including spirituals, Native American music, popular tunes and a composition by Arizona State University music professor James DeMars.

location: 6947 E. McDonald Drive Paradise Valley, AZ, 85253
name: Choir Performance
description: The ASU Women’s and Men’s Choruses join to present an evening of choral music.

name: Piano Concerto Festival: Grieg Piano Concerto in A Minor
description: The Phoenix Symphony's Piano Concerto Festival kicks off with Norwegian composer Edvard Grieg's best known work, the dynamic Piano Concerto in A Minor, along with incidental music composed by Grieg for the play "Peer Gynt."

name: Piano Concerto Festival
description: This one-hour program features selections from Edvard Grieg's Piano Concerto in A Minor and Tchaikovsky’s Piano Concerto No. 1.

name: Phoenix Boys Choir: "The Great American Songbook"
description: The choir presents a salute to the great American songwriters, covering six decades of America’s most popular jazz, blues, Broadway, folk, rock and Motown songs. The concert kicks off with the music of Cole Porter, Irving Berlin and George and Ira Gershwin, and leads into works of Richard Rogers, Leonard Bernstein and Stephen Sondheim. The shows goes on to include songs by Bill Haley, Billy Joel, Duke Ellington and Paul Simon.

name: Piano Concerto Festival: Tchaikovsky Piano Concerto No. 1
description: The Phoenix Symphony presents Tchaikovsky’s acclaimed Piano Concerto No. 1, paired with the composer’s "Serenade for Strings" and Voyevoda, op. 78.

location: 4027 E. Lincoln Drive Paradise Valley, AZ, 85253
name: The Mozart Affair
description: The "Four Seasons Orchestra" performs an all-Mozart concert. Featured selections include the Piano Concerto No. 20, Flute Concerto No. 1., Sinfonia Concertante for Violin and Viola and Jupiter Symphony No. 41. Sponsored by Scottsdale League for the Arts, Arizona Commission on the Arts and the Four Seasons Orchestra of Scottsdale.

name: North Valley Chorale: "Peace Offerings"
description: The chorale performs its final concert of the season, singing "Dona Nobis Pacem" by Vaughan Williams, accompanied by psalms, songs and poems of peace.

name: "Maestros in Concert: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma and Zakir Hussain"
description: Internationally recognized and award-winning Indian artists Pandit Shivkumar Sharma and Zakir Hussain perform classical music of India.

name: Paradise on Broadway: A Musical Revue
description: Students in the college's Musical Theater Workshop sing some of the most famous hits from Broadway, Hollywood and television. The performance is in the Studio Theatre, M-East building.

name: "Mother's Day at the Opera"
description: Celebrate Mother's Day with operatic selections courtesy of the Symphony of the Southwest.

name: Freedom Rock Experience
description: Consider the Source, the Phoenix-based rock band, will perform with their guests, the East Valley Youth Symphony and dancers from the Dance Barn. Proceeds from the concert will go to Operation Homefront of Arizona, benefiting the nation's heroes. Other special guests in the audience will be Snowball Express families from Arizona. The Snowball children have lost a parent in the wars in Iraq or Afghanistan.

name: "Popera"
description: This performance is a blend of popular, spiritual and classical songs, featuring the stars of the Phoenix Opera with a special guest appearance by international opera star Robert Hale. Accompanied by the Phoenix Opera Orchestra. Proceeds benefit the opera.

location: 6947 E. McDonald Drive Paradise Valley, AZ, 85253
name: "Crossing Paths"
description: The Sonoran Desert Chorale closes out its season with this spirited concert, which features music the group will perform on their upcoming annual international tour, which includes stops in Austria, Hungary and Slovenia.

location: 9502 W. Hutton Drive Sun City, AZ, 85351
name: "Popera"
venue: All Saints of the Desert Episcopal Church
description: This performance is a blend of popular, spiritual and classical songs, featuring the stars of the Phoenix Opera with a special guest appearance by international opera star Robert Hale. Accompanied by the Phoenix Opera Orchestra. Proceeds benefit the opera.

name: Classical Ensembles Concert
description: Hear music classics performed by Paradise Valley Community College's classical-music ensemble featuring choir, flute ensemble, orchestra, percussion and piano. This performance is held in the college's Center for Performing Arts.

name: Hoodstock
description: Seven bands are scheduled to play, including Groove Noodles, What's Left and Small Leaks Sink Ships. Entertainment begins at 5 p.m. on Friday and 3:30 p.m. on Saturday. Artwork created by children on vinyl records is sold. Hoodstock sponsors are Hoodums Music & Movies, Changing Hands Bookstore, Mac’s Broiler and Tap, and Bobbi’s Flowers. Each will donate a percentage of sales to Broadmor Elementary's Academic Intervention Program, which assists children with help outside the classroom. Co-sponsor Moses Anshell Advertising is donating T-shirts and posters, with all proceeds going to the school. Visit website for details.

location: 700 W. Rio Salado Parkway Tempe, AZ, 85281
name: Carolyn Eynon Singers
description: Guest soprano Yolanda Rhodes joins 24 singers to present "Songs of the American Spirit." The group performs all-American spirituals, folk songs, opera, gospel and barbershop numbers by Copland, Bernstein, Hogan, Hayes, Mulholland, Berlin, Shaw and Rey.

location: 38410 N. School House Road Cave Creek, AZ, 85331
name: Cave Creek Thieves Market
description: Shoppers can find a unique gift at this open-air flea market with a special "Mom Knows Best" theme. Choices include jewelry, clothing, gourmet dog biscuits and garage-sale items. Live alternative, bluegrass and folk music is performed by the six-member, Tempe band O'Henry. Held in the tamarisk grove. (Photo courtesy Cave Creek Thieves Market)

location: 9445 E. Doubletree Ranch Road Scottsdale, AZ, 85258
name: Steal the Scenery
description: This four-piece alternative group from California draws inspiration from the sounds of sounds of Elvis Presley and Michael Jackson. The group mixes together catchy, radio-ready guitar hooks and dance melodies with an energetic performance and raspy vocals for a wide audience appeal. Their first album, "All or Nothing," was released last year.

location: 420 N. Florence St. Casa Grande, AZ, 85222
name: Cinco de Mayo Weekend Bash
description: Head to Casa Grande for rap, hip-hop and Latino music performances. Performers include Glasses Malone, Da Beast, Mob Fam and Rich Rico. Call or visit website to purchase tickets. An all-ages event.

name: Donor Drive and Concert
description: Learn how to become a marrow stem-cell donor and help people battling blood cancers and diseases. Sign up that day to become a donor. A concert featuring “Betty” follows the donor drive at 8 p.m.

name: B/S - The Tribute to Bon Scott-era AC/DC
description: This Phoenix band pays tribute to the Bon Scott-era of AC/DC, re-creating the look and sound of the Australian metal legends 1979 live show. The band performs hits such as “High Voltage,” “Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap” and “It's a Long Way to the Top (If You Wanna Rock 'n' Roll).”

name: Kansas
description: These classic rockers scored hits in the 1970s with songs such as "Carry On Wayward Son" and "Dust in the Wind," landing them two multi-platinum albums and five gold albums. The group's latest album, "Somewhere to Elsewhere," marked the reunion of the band's original 1970s lineup.

name: Cinderella
description: These Philadelphia glam rockers were a huge hit in the mid-1980s, with their first three albums going platinum and scoring hits such as "Nobody's Fool," "Don't Know What You Got (Till It's Gone)" and "Coming Home." The group arrives as part of its 25th Anniversary Tour. Rockers Sludge's Build a Band open this all-ages show.

name: A Perfect Circle
description: This alternative metal supergroup returns to the Valley following a long hiatus and a string of small reunion shows in 2010, including three dates at the Marquee Theater in Tempe. The group features Maynard James Keenan of Tool, Billy Howerdel of Ashes Divide, James Iha of the Smashing Pumpkins, Josh Freese of Devo and Matt McJunkins of Puscifer. The band has released three albums, 2000's "Mer de Noms," 2003's "Thirteenth Step" and 2004's "Emotive.

name: Musical Jam Session for Musicians with Memory Loss
description: The Banner Alzheimer’s Institute and the ASU Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts offers a free monthly “jam session” designed for musicians with memory loss issues. Participants and care partners are invited to bring their instruments to play or to sing along. Some instruments, including pianos, guitars and drums, are provided by ASU. Jams are held the first Friday of each month. Registration required.

name: Def Leppard
description: These English heavy-metal legends return to the Valley, playing songs from throughout their career as well tunes from their new live album, 2011's "Mirrorball." Emerging as part of the new wave of British heavy metal movement of the late 1970s, Def Leppard scored radio hits such as "Love Bites," "Pour Some Sugar on Me" and "Photograph"; albums "Hysteria" and "Pyromania" have sold more than 10 million copies each. Seattle rock legends Heart also perform at this all-ages show.

name: The Noodles
description: Sunday afternoons, the Sail Inn plays home to this Grateful Dead tribute band. The Noodles play their improv heavy renditions of the Dead's best songs, attracting a faithful following of Deadheads.

name: Compassion Fundraiser
description: The benefit features a custom motorcycle show and a performance by Christian rapper the Rep. Gold and jewelry items are collected, A silent auction, kids activities and a raffle are included. Barbecue items are available from D'Vine's chef Ramon Rice. Proceeds benefit Jim, a man battling end-stage renal failure, his wife Diana, a preschool teacher at Bridges Preschool in Mesa, and their four children. Admission includes 12 raffle tickets.

name: Cinco de Mayo
description: Mex and Match food specials, normally $8.99, include tacos, enchiladas, tamales, burros, tostadas or chile rellenos and two side choices of Mexican rice, black beans, refried beans, vegetables or a cup of soup. Drink specials include $2 for Coors Light bottles or drafts, $3 for Corona, Corona Light or Pacifico and $5 for a 16-ounce Margarita de Macayo. A variety of live bands perform rock music from noon to midnight.

name: Heart and Soul Sounds of Arizona
description: After a long day at work, come out to to relax by the stage and listen to some hot R&B artists while enjoying drink specials until midnight. Age 21-and-older event. Presented by Babyangel R&B Promotions

name: Soul School Jam 1
description: This concert features the ‘80s R&B “S.O.S. Band”; Rose Royce, known for the ‘70s disco-era hit “Car Wash”; Tom Browne, the jazz trumpeter; and Brick, which offers a fusion of funk, jazz, disco and R&B . Tickets available online or at the box office. (Photo courtesy of Celebrity Theatre)

name: Guy Pennacchio
description: This stylish singer pays tribute to the music of Frank Sinatra, singing songs such as "Fly Me To the Moon," "My Way" and "Witchcraft."

name: Dan Zanes and Friends
venue: Scottsdale Center for the Performing Arts
description: The former singer of the roots-rock band the Del Fuegos heads up this band, which performs fun, family oriented music that not only includes the traditional rock instruments - guitar, bass and drums - but others, such as the tuba, accordion, pump organ, djembe and saw. (Photo courtesy Arthur Elgort)

name: Katy Perry
description: This pop superstar arrives in the Valley as part of her worldwide California Dreams tour. The California singer first hit the mainstream with her No. 1 2008 hit, "I Kissed a Girl." Perry's third album, 2010's "Teenage Dream," debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 chart and spawned the hit singles "California Gurls," "Teenage Dream" and "Firework." The album is also nominated for album of the year and best pop vocal album at the 53rd Grammy Awards.
